result.family: cross-sectional / relative-value (XS momentum, XS short-term reversal, residual momentum vs BTC, BTC-gated long-only alt rotation, ETH/BTC + SOL/BTC ratio-trend pairs)
result.summary:
I wrote PLAN.md before looking at any out-of-sample (OOS) number. I tested 142 in-sample (IS) variants across five families on daily Binance perp bars using the shared harness timing and costs. I took 3 finalists to OOS, once each.

Result: one passes P1-P8 as written, but it is a weak pass. Two fail.

**D, BTC-gated long-only alt rotation (PASS, weak).** Rule: hold the top 3 coins by 7-day return, but only while BTC closes above its 50-day SMA. Sized at a constant 0.244x of equity (20% IS vol target).
- IS Sharpe 2.28, OOS Sharpe 0.59, OOS +24.4% (+15.5% at 2x costs), max drawdown 20.8%.
- P6 neighbours: median OOS Sharpe 0.47, 89% positive.
- Correlation with the desk 0.23 over the full period (0.34 OOS). A 50/50 blend has OOS Sharpe 0.89 vs the desk's 0.85.
- Caveats:
  - The OOS t-stat is only about 1.0.
  - 2025 was -6.6%.
  - Post-OOS check: simply holding BTC under the same gate at the same sizing did better OOS (Sharpe 0.88, drawdown 7%, blend 0.97). So OOS the alt-picking part added nothing over BTC.
  - The momentum ranking does beat random picks under the same gate (OOS Sharpe -0.28 on average).
  - Survivorship bias did not explain the OOS result: an early-12-coin universe gave OOS Sharpe 0.60.
  - At $50 and 0.244x, each of the 3 slots is about $4, below Hyperliquid's ~$10 minimum order. It needs about $125 or more per account.

**A, market-neutral cross-sectional momentum (FAIL).** 28-day lookback, long top 5 / short bottom 5, daily rebalance.
- IS Sharpe 1.44, then OOS Sharpe 0.18, +4.5% net and -9.8% at 2x costs.
- P6 median -0.09, only 29% of neighbours positive.
- Costs took about 3/4 of the gross OOS profit.

**E, ETH/BTC + SOL/BTC ratio trend, up-only (FAIL).**
- IS Sharpe 1.40 (almost all from 2021), then OOS Sharpe -0.17, -5.3%.
- All 8 neighbours were negative OOS.

**Families with no finalist.**
- Short-term reversal is negative in every IS variant.
- Residual momentum ranked 4th on robust IS score, close to A, so it was not taken to OOS under the 3-finalist cap.

Book multiplied by constant m=0.2436 (chosen on IS: 20% vol target), i.e. ~8.1% of equity per coin. Fill at the next day's open, hold through that day. candidates.notes: Weak pass. P2 margin is thin: OOS Sharpe 0.586 vs the 0.5 bar, t-stat about 0.97 over 2.75 years. OOS 2x-cost Sharpe 0.41. Per year at 0.244x: 2020 +51%, 2021 +140%, 2022 -10%, 2023 +75%, 2024 +15%, 2025 -6.6%, 2026 YTD +15.7% (the desk's BTC strategy is -11% in 2026). OOS correlation with the desk 0.34. Turnover about 36x/yr OOS; OOS cost drag 7.4%; funding paid 3.2% OOS and 11.7% IS. Post-OOS diagnostics (not used for selection): (1) BTC-only under the same SMA50 gate at the same sizing had OOS Sharpe 0.88, +21%, drawdown 7%, and a 50/50 desk blend of 0.97, so OOS the rotation does not beat simply holding BTC under its own gate. (2) Equal-weight all-coin basket under the gate: OOS Sharpe 0.25. Random 3 coins under the gate: mean -0.28 (20 seeds, max 0.17). So momentum ranking beats random alt picks, but alts as a whole lagged BTC. (3) Universe limited to the 12 coins listed by 2020-02-15 (less survivorship): OOS Sharpe 0.60. (4) Leave-one-coin-out OOS Sharpe ranges from 0.31 (DOGE removed) to 0.75. Top OOS contributors were XLM, DOGE, XRP and SUI. Unlevered the book has 54-70% drawdown and about 82% vol. At $50 and 0.244x each slot is about $4, below Hyperliquid's ~$10 minimum order, so it needs about $125 or more per account. Binance funding was used, not Hyperliquid's hourly funding.

Post-OOS diagnostic: an equal-weight basket of all eligible coins under the same BTC>SMA50 gate had IS Sharpe 1.88 but OOS 0.25; holding 3 random eligible coins under the gate had OOS Sharpe -0.28 on average (20 seeds). Owning alts as a group under a BTC trend filter has not paid since 2024.
observations: Market-neutral cross-sectional books (A, C) have about zero daily correlation with the current desk (-0.05 to +0.08 IS). If one ever works it diversifies well, but large-cap XS momentum lost its edge after 2023: OOS gross edge about +7%/yr, roughly 3/4 of it lost to 7.5 bps/side costs at daily rebalancing.
Crypto 1-3 day cross-sectional returns trend rather than reverse: the reversal family was negative in every variant. Never fade the daily cross-sectional winners.

Post-OOS diagnostic only (not a pre-registered candidate): a trivial 'long BTC when the daily close is above its 50-day SMA' at 0.24x had OOS Sharpe 0.88 (2024-26) with a 7% drawdown, about equal to the desk's own OOS Sharpe of 0.85. IS Sharpe was 1.17 vs the desk BTC's 1.41. OOS correlation with the desk is 0.51, and a 50/50 blend with the desk had OOS Sharpe 0.97. It would need its own IS-first test before any use; it suggests the 2h breakout's complexity buys little OOS.
The D rotation's 2026 YTD is +15.7% while the desk's BTC strategy is about -11%. D's daily correlation with the desk BTC account is 0.27 OOS, so it diversifies, but it lost 6.6% in 2025.

Survivorship: the 25-coin list was picked in 2026. In-sample, D's results are dominated by 2021 coins that are on the list because they survived and grew (SOL, AVAX, NEAR, DOGE). Practical sizing problem: at $50 per account with the 0.244x size the 20% vol target needs, each of 3 slots is about $4, below Hyperliquid's roughly $10 minimum order. Rotation books need about $125 or more per account, or must run at 3-4x the safe size (50-70% drawdowns unlevered).

Funding matters for long-alt books: D paid 11.7% of equity in funding over 2020-23 even at 0.24x (about 0.5x equity per 4 years at 1x). Shorts in market-neutral books collected small net funding (A paid -0.9% IS, i.e. received).
ETH/BTC and SOL/BTC ratio trend following made almost all its money in 2021. Since 2024 the up-only signal whipsaws (OOS -5%), and the ETH/BTC ratio has spent most of 2024-26 in a downtrend.

result.family: diversified trend-following (desk breakout on 20 coins; vol-targeted daily TSMOM ensembles; BTC-regime filter for alts)
result.summary:
Short answer: running the desk's own 2h breakout on 20 coins fails, even in-sample. A different trend signal across the same 20 coins does work out of sample: a daily, volatility-scaled momentum ensemble (TSMOM: hold each coin in the direction of its recent returns, sized by its volatility). It passes P1-P8 in two versions, and it works best as a complement to the desk, not a replacement.

I wrote PLAN.md before looking at any out-of-sample number. 97 variants were tried in-sample, 3 finalists went to out-of-sample once each, and nothing was re-tuned afterwards.

(a) Desk breakout on 20 coins. Rules: 60-bar Donchian breakout, EMA100/400 filter, 3-ATR(28) stop and chandelier trail, trend-flip exit, 1% risk per coin, 3x gross cap. My own simulator checks stops intrabar against bar high/low; on BTC alone its daily returns correlate 0.91 with the desk baseline. Results: in-sample Sharpe 0.31-0.42 with drawdowns of 58-82%. The 27-point parameter cube tops out at 0.53. Shorts are worse. 11 of the 20 coins lose money. Fees plus funding (0.44 + 0.47 cumulative) eat about two thirds of the 1.35 gross P&L. Rejected in-sample; not taken out of sample.

(b) TSMOM ensemble. Daily bars; each coin's signal is the mean of sign(return) over 7/14/28/56/112-day lookbacks. Position = signal x 0.40 / the coin's 40-day volatility / number of coins, scaled to a portfolio volatility target, with a 20% no-trade band. In-sample Sharpe was 1.27-1.65 long-only and 0.94-1.12 long/short. I took the pre-declared base settings, not the top scorer.
- F1, 20 coins, long-only, 30% vol target: in-sample Sharpe 1.57. Out-of-sample Sharpe 0.94, +100%, max drawdown 34.0% (just under the 35% limit), +80% at double costs. All 26 neighbours are positive out of sample (median Sharpe 0.83). Correlation with the desk is 0.49; a 50/50 blend has Sharpe 1.04 vs the desk's 0.85. PASS.
- F2, same rules long/short, 20% vol target: in-sample 1.12. Out-of-sample Sharpe 0.75, +52%, drawdown 25.6%, +38% at double costs. Neighbour median 0.72, 26/26 positive. Correlation with the desk 0.25; blend 1.00. PASS.
- F3, F1's rules on BTC/ETH/SOL only: in-sample 2.17, out-of-sample 0.75, but drawdown 38.4%, so it FAILS P7.

(c) The BTC-uptrend filter for alts adds nothing robust (about +/-0.05 Sharpe in most variants).

Breadth is not a free lunch. In-sample, Sharpe goes down as small alts are added (3 coins 2.21 > 10 coins 2.03 > 20 coins 1.62 > 17 non-desk coins 1.24). Out of sample the 20-coin version did better than the 3-coin one (0.94 vs 0.75) and had a smaller drawdown.

Caveats that matter:
- One extra day of execution delay cuts out-of-sample Sharpe to 0.68 (F1) and 0.49 (F2).
- TRX is the biggest out-of-sample contributor; without it Sharpe is 0.76 / 0.67.
- On the 5 newer coins (SUI/APT/ARB/OP/INJ, out of sample only) the same rules are flat (Sharpe 0.16 / 0.12).
- The coin list was picked in 2026, which flatters long-only most.
- The median position is 1.5-3% of equity across 9-20 coins, with 1,650-2,850 orders a year. On $150 with Hyperliquid's $10 minimum order this cannot be traded; it needs roughly $2-5k or more.

candidates.name: tsmom20_long
candidates.rules: Data: Binance USDT-M perp daily candles (00:00 UTC bars, H.klines(c,'1d')), real funding. Universe: BTC ETH SOL BNB XRP DOGE ADA AVAX LINK DOT LTC BCH TRX ATOM NEAR UNI AAVE FIL ETC XLM (a coin trades once its indicators are warm). Signal at each daily close t, per coin: s = mean over L in {7,14,28,56,112} days of sign(close_t/close_{t-L} - 1); long-only, so s is clipped at 0. sigma_ann = std of the last 40 daily returns x sqrt(365). Raw weight = s x 0.40 / sigma_ann / N_eligible. Portfolio scaler k_t = 0.30 / (std of the raw portfolio's last 60 daily returns (raw weights at t-1 x returns at t) x sqrt(365)), clipped to [0,4]; target = raw x k; total gross capped at 3x by proportional scaling. No-trade band: a coin's held weight changes only if |target - held| > 0.2 x |target|, or the sign changes, or target or held is 0. Timing: decide at daily close t, fill at open t+1 (harness backtest_portfolio); 7.5 bps per side on |delta weight|; funding paid on held weight. No stops, no take-profit; exits happen when the signal goes to 0.

Caveats: (1) survivorship-biased universe, which flatters long-only most; (2) one extra day of execution delay drops OOS Sharpe to 0.68; (3) TRX is the largest OOS contributor (ex-TRX Sharpe 0.76, +68%); (4) frozen rules on the 2022-23 listings (SUI APT ARB OP INJ) were flat out of sample (Sharpe 0.16, drawdown 39%); (5) OOS beta to BTC 0.30, correlation 0.44; (6) not executable at $150: the median coin weight is 2.9% of equity (about $4) and there are about 1,650 orders a year, so it needs roughly $2-5k or more given the $10 minimum order; check that every coin is listed on Hyperliquid; (7) 97 in-sample trials, though the finalist was the pre-declared base setting, not the best in-sample scorer (1.65).

negative_results: Desk breakout (2h, N60, EMA100/400, 3-ATR stop+trail, trend-flip exit, intrabar stops) on 20 coins, 1% risk per coin, 3x gross cap, long-only: in-sample Sharpe 0.31, +15%, drawdown 66%, 1,567 entries. Fails P3 badly.
Same with the BTC regime gate on alt entries: in-sample 0.34 (drawdown 58%); gate + exit alts when BTC flips: 0.35 (drawdown 59%).
Same long/short (mirror breakdowns): in-sample 0.37 / 0.42 / 0.42 (none / gate / gate+exit) with drawdowns of 79-82%. Shorts add trades, not edge.
Same long-only without the gross cap: in-sample 0.14, -19%, drawdown 73%.

27-point cube N{40,60,90} x k{2.5,3,4} x EMA{50/200,100/400,150/600} (gate+exit): long best 0.53 (N40 k4 100/400), all 27 between -0.01 and 0.53, drawdowns 46-75%; long/short all between -0.05 and 0.42, drawdowns 77-94%. No region reaches 0.7.

Per-coin desk breakout in-sample: only BTC (1.32), ADA (0.90), FIL (0.87), ETH (0.80), BNB (0.55) clearly positive; 11 of 20 coins negative (ATOM -1.03, UNI -0.97, LTC -0.92). Gross P&L 1.35 vs fees 0.44 + funding 0.47.
BTC-uptrend gate for alt longs inside TSMOM: Sharpe change of -0.06 to +0.06 in 10 of 12 pairs, +0.14 only at the doubled lookbacks. Not robust, not adopted.
TSMOM on 4h bars (lookbacks x6): in-sample 1.59 long / 1.04 long-short vs 1.62 / 1.12 daily, with 2x the cost. No gain.
TSMOM z-scored (clipped return/vol) signal instead of sign: in-sample 1.55 vs 1.62 long (base lookbacks), 1.11 vs 1.12 long-short. No gain.
TSMOM doubled lookbacks {14..224}d: in-sample 1.27 long / 0.95 long-short, below the base set; halved {4..56}d: 1.57 / 1.03, about the same.
TSMOM long-only on the 17 non-desk coins: in-sample 1.24, below the 20-coin 1.62 and 3-coin 2.21. The small alts dilute.
F1/F2 frozen rules on the 2022-23 listings SUI APT ARB OP INJ (extra holdout, OOS only): Sharpe 0.16 (+0.7%, drawdown 39%) and 0.12 (+0.5%, drawdown 33%). No edge on the newer coins.
F3 (TSMOM long-only on BTC/ETH/SOL, 30% vol target): out-of-sample drawdown 38.4%, fails P7; in-sample 2.17 fell to 0.75 out of sample.
Timing robustness (diagnostic only): one extra day of execution delay cuts out-of-sample Sharpe from 0.94 to 0.68 (F1) and from 0.75 to 0.49 (F2).
observations: Breadth is not where the edge is for the desk's breakout rules. On 20 coins those rules lose to BTC alone in-sample (0.31-0.53 vs 1.31). Alt breakouts on 2h bars whipsaw, and funding on long alts (very high in 2021) eats about a third of gross P&L.

The trend signal matters more than breadth. A daily, volatility-scaled TSMOM ensemble (1-16 week lookbacks) beats the 2h Donchian+stop design on the same coins by a wide margin in-sample (1.62 vs 0.31 long-only), with about 3x less cost per unit of exposure.

Across 20 coins the wider 4-ATR stop beat 3-ATR in every in-sample cube row for the breakout. That backs up the earlier post-hoc 4-ATR finding for ETH/SOL, though the breakout portfolio still fails overall.

Complementarity is the real value. Out of sample, the desk made +24% in 2025 when F1 was -6% and F2 -17%. In 2024 and 2026 YTD the TSMOM books made +73%/+23% (F1) and +35%/+36% (F2) while the desk made +13%/+4%. Desk+F1 50/50: OOS Sharpe 1.04, drawdown 22%. Desk+F2 50/50: 1.00, drawdown 16%. Desk+F1+F2 in thirds: 1.08, drawdown 19.7%. Desk alone: 0.85, drawdown 14.7%.

F2 (long/short TSMOM) is the most different return stream found: OOS correlation 0.25 with the desk, beta to BTC -0.13. Long-only F1 is partly crypto beta (beta 0.30, correlation 0.44 to BTC), but it beat BTC buy-and-hold Sharpe (0.94 vs 0.76) and equal-weight buy-and-hold of the 20 coins (0.44) out of sample.

In-sample Sharpe fell as coins were added (3 coins 2.21 > 10 coins 2.03 > 20 coins 1.62). Out of sample it reversed (20 coins 0.94 vs 3 coins 0.75) with a smaller drawdown (34% vs 38%). The 3-coin in-sample result was inflated by the 2020-21 BTC/ETH/SOL run.

Practical blocker: the desk cannot run a 20-coin book on 3 x $50. Median per-coin weight is 2.9% (F1) or 1.5% (F2) of equity, median rebalance 2.2% / 1.2%, with about 1,650 / 2,850 orders a year, against Hyperliquid's $10 minimum order. That implies roughly $2-5k or more of equity. If the desk wants this, the smallest honest step is paper-trading F2 or F1 with a larger notional paper balance, or widening the no-trade band (not tested out of sample).
The TSMOM edge depends on executing at the daily close (00:00 UTC). Waiting an extra day cuts Sharpe by about 0.25, so a live version must rebalance promptly after the UTC daily close.
Concentration: TRX was the largest out-of-sample contributor (Dec-2024 spike). Without TRX, OOS Sharpe is 0.76 (F1) and 0.67 (F2), still above 0.5.

Survivorship: the 25-coin universe was picked in 2026, and dead 2020-era majors (LUNA, FTT, EOS, XTZ...) are missing. This flatters long-only F1 most. The newer-coin holdout came out flat, a warning that the edge may be weaker on coins that are not long-surviving majors.

result.summary: Nothing in this family survives out of sample. I looked at 1,153 cells and variants on 2020-23 data only: about 553 simulated rules and about 600 descriptive cells, logged in trials.log. PLAN.md, which fixes the rules, grids and neighbour grids, was written before any out-of-sample number was computed. Three finalists went to out-of-sample, once each, and all three FAIL the pass rule. (1) cb_sol, "crash-bounce": buy SOL for 2h after BTC's 3h move falls below -3 sigma. In-sample Sharpe 2.24; out-of-sample Sharpe -0.18 (-5.8%), -17% at 2x costs, and all 4 neighbours negative out of sample. (2) tom_ew3, turn of month: hold BTC/ETH/SOL over the last 4 days and first 5 days of each month. In-sample Sharpe 1.95, positive in every in-sample year, and first of 32 placebo month offsets. Out of sample the effect reversed: Sharpe -1.10, -45%, max drawdown 54%, and every out-of-sample year was negative. (3) cb_alts, the same crash-bounce trigger on a 19-alt basket: in-sample 1.44, out-of-sample -0.68 (-24%). Below the finalists: hour-of-day effects are real but tiny (3-5 bps per hour against 15 bps per round trip), and 0 of 144 hour-window rules reach in-sample Sharpe 0.7. Blocking desk entries by hour or weekday gains at most +0.10 Sharpe in-sample out of 44 variants (noise level), and blocking entries just before funding prints hurts. Fading the CME weekend gap loses in all 24 variants. Day-of-week and Deribit-expiry effects are not consistent across years. Lead-lag at 1h is too small after costs: the clear 1h lead-lag finding is that SOL over-reacts to BTC moves and then partly reverses, and all of that profit was the buy-after-a-crash side, which then failed out of sample. Recommendation: add nothing from this family to the desk. The one IS-supported finding about desk timing (hour/weekday entry blocks) was within noise and was not tested out of sample.

candidates.rules: Data: Binance USDT-M perp 1h bars (harness H.klines), real funding (H.bar_funding). BTC's k-h move had a negative IC with SOL's next hour, consistent across all 4 IS years; the profit was all on the long side, so it was turned into a long-only crash-bounce. IS: 35/36 SOL grid variants >= 0.7, and 34/34 confirmation runs on 17 other pre-2021 coins positive. Per year: 2020 +15%, 2021 +179%, 2022 +19%, 2023 +13%, 2024 +22%, 2025 -16%, 2026 -8%. The edge seems to have faded after 2024 (more market-making, fewer liquidation cascades) and was heavily driven by 2021. Survivorship flatters a buy-the-crash rule (LUNA and FTT are not in the universe). Uncorrelated with the desk (-0.01), but the OOS return is negative. Any hunter can reuse it to test entry gates without touching the repo.

Hour-of-day (IS 2020-23, 20 pre-2021 coins): only 02:00 and 09:00 UTC are same-sign in all 4 IS years and confirmed in the other 17 coins, both negative (demeaned -5.0 and -2.9 bps/hour, t -3.2 / -1.9). No hour is consistently positive. Hourly vol is highest at 00 UTC and 12-15 UTC (US open; 120-129 bps) and lowest at 04-07 UTC (88-94 bps). These effects are an order of magnitude below the 15 bps round-trip cost; at most they are execution-timing trivia for the multi-day desk, not a strategy. None of this was checked out of sample.

The desk's IS trades split by signal hour or weekday show no stable pattern. Entry-time gates are within noise IS, so I see no reason to delay or skip entries by clock time. Blocking entries just before funding prints actively hurt in-sample. Note that Hyperliquid pays funding hourly, so Binance's 00/08/16 print-hour effects would not carry over anyway.

SOL over-reacts to BTC moves at the 1-3h horizon. BTC's past 1-3h return has a negative IC (-0.03 to -0.04, all 4 IS years) with SOL's next hour; part of this is SOL's own short-term reversal (own IC -0.02..-0.03). The tradeable part was 'buy SOL after a BTC crash', which worked through 2024 and then lost money in 2025-26.

Calendar effects that looked strongest in-sample (turn of month: IS Sharpe 1.95, positive every year, placebo rank 1/32) reversed sharply out of sample (2024-26 every year negative). With ~1,150 cells examined, any calendar pattern found in the 2020-23 bull/bear sample should be treated as presumed noise. This includes the 'month-end flows' and 'weekend' folklore.

Both crash-bounce finalists had ~0 correlation with the desk (-0.01 / -0.03), so a working short-horizon mean-reversion sleeve would diversify. It would need a mechanism that still exists after 2024; this one does not.

Survivorship: the universe was picked in 2026, which biases any buy-the-crash or alt-basket result upward (LUNA, FTT and other crash casualties are absent). This matters most for the crash-bounce family.
Harness note: H.stats needs an 'h' column to count entries; for H.backtest_portfolio results I set h = gross_exposure.

result.summary:
I tested 109 rule variants. All of them were chosen on 2020-23 data only. Three finalists were then run once each on 2024-01 to 2026-09.

(1) Cross-sectional funding carry (xs_carry). Each day, short the 3 of 25 perps with the highest 7-day average funding and long the 3 with the lowest, at 0.6x gross. In-sample Sharpe 1.09 (+129%, max drawdown 23%). Out-of-sample Sharpe 0.88, +39%, max drawdown 10%. At 2x costs it still made +17%. Its correlation with the desk is -0.01, and a 50/50 blend with the desk has an out-of-sample Sharpe of 1.28 against 0.85 for the desk alone. It PASSES P1-P8 as written. Two big caveats. First, the coin list was picked today, so it only holds coins that survived. The long leg buys the lowest-funding coins, and dying coins like LUNA and FTT had very negative funding before they collapsed, so they are missing. A real 2022 would likely have been about 20 points worse. Second, 2026 so far is only +1.4%.

(2) Spot-vs-perp carry (cash_carry): long spot plus short perp on BTC/ETH/SOL whenever 7-day funding is above 10% a year, exit below 5%. In-sample Sharpe 7.8, CAGR 13%. Out-of-sample Sharpe 6.8, but only +11.8% in total (4.1% a year), max drawdown 0.3%. It had only 16 out-of-sample entries (the rule needs 20), so it is PLAUSIBLE, not PASS. The yield on Binance funding is roughly what T-bills pay. As a descriptive check (not a validated result), the same rule on Hyperliquid funding made +49.8% from 2023-06 to 2026-09, against +15.0% on Binance funding, because Hyperliquid funding runs about twice as high.

(3) A relative crowding gate on the real desk engine (rel_crowding): block a long when 3-day funding is above its own trailing one-year 90th percentile, instead of the fixed ~52%/yr line. In-sample the desk Sharpe went from 1.52 to 1.67. Out-of-sample it went from 0.852 to 0.878, while return slipped from 46.2% to 45.2%. Its neighbours scored 0.92 and 1.02. It PASSES by the letter, through the blend test (0.875 vs 0.852), but the out-of-sample gain is within noise: ETH and SOL improved, BTC got worse.

What did not work: using funding or the premium index as a contrarian timing signal for BTC/ETH/SOL. Extreme negative funding was followed by further falls, not short squeezes. All 36 short-on-extreme variants lost money or were near zero in-sample.

How much funding the desk pays: BTC paid $69 in funding against $85 in fees over 2020-26, about 8% of gross trade profit. The desk holds a position only about 12% of the time, so funding is a small cost and not the cause of the 2026 losses. Hyperliquid funding is systematically higher than Binance's, about 14% vs 7% a year on BTC/ETH from 2023-05 to 2026-09. That adds about 1.2% a year of cost to the BTC account and makes carry trades on Hyperliquid more attractive.

candidates.name: xs_carry
candidates.coins: 25 Binance USDT-M perps (harness UNIVERSE; coins enter after 60 days of funding history). Survivorship-biased.
candidates.params: L=7 days funding lookback, k=3 per side, rebalance R=1 day, dollar-neutral (beta-neutral off), gross 0.6x (0.1x per leg)
candidates.rules: Data: Binance daily perp bars (00:00 UTC). Funding per day = sum of prints in (open, close] (H.bar_funding '1d'), known at the close. Signal = rolling 7-day mean of the daily funding sums. Eligible coins that day: at least 60 days since the first funding print, a close that day, and a signal value; at least 6 eligible coins needed. At each daily close: short the 3 highest-signal coins at -0.5/3 each and long the 3 lowest at +0.5/3 each, then multiply all weights by 0.6, so gross 0.6x and each leg 0.1x of equity. Fill at the next open and hold one day. Rebalance daily. Costs: 7.5 bps per side on each weight change only (unchanged legs cost nothing; no drift rebalancing charged). Real Binance funding is paid or received on each leg. No stops. Market-neutral: beta to the equal-weight universe is -0.01 in-sample and -0.04 out-of-sample.
candidates.failed_rules: none (P1-P8 all met as written)
candidates.notes: Leverage: 0.6x gross. Yearly returns: 2020 +10.7%, 2021 +81.9%, 2022 +7.6%, 2023 +5.8%, 2024 +11.9%, 2025 +22.6%, 2026 YTD +1.4%. Out-of-sample P&L sums: price +0.39, funding received +0.14, costs -0.17; the long leg did most of the work. Neighbours' out-of-sample Sharpe: L3 0.14, L14 0.95, k5 0.95, R3 0.70. Two cautions about the selection. First, my original in-sample pick (L3,k5,R1, in-sample Sharpe 1.21) made all its money in 2021 (2022 -13%, 2023 -10%), so before looking at any out-of-sample number I changed the selection rule to 'positive Sharpe in every in-sample year, then the best full in-sample Sharpe'. Only 2 of the 48 cells passed that filter. Second, survivorship bias: the long leg buys the lowest-funding coins, and coins that later died (LUNA in May 2022, FTT in Nov 2022) had very negative funding before collapsing. They are not in the universe, so the real 2022 result would likely be about 20 points worse. Practical limits: 6 legs at 0.1x is $5 per leg on a $50 account, below Hyperliquid's $10 minimum order, so it needs at least $100 per account (realistically $200 or more). Tested on Binance's funding cross-section only; Hyperliquid's has not been tested. Turnover is about 415 leg entries a year.

candidates.name: cash_carry
candidates.coins: BTC, ETH, SOL (Binance spot + Binance perp)
candidates.params: enter above 10% APR, exit below 5% APR, lookback 7 days (21 prints), 1x spot plus 1x short perp, one third of equity per coin
candidates.rules: 8h bars aligned to the funding prints (00/08/16 UTC). Per coin: APR = mean of the last 21 funding sums per 8h bar x 3 x 365 x 100. State machine: enter when APR > 10 (spot leg +1/3 of equity, perp leg -1/3); exit both legs when APR < 5. Decide at the bar close, fill at the next open. Each leg pays 7.5 bps per side on changes. The short perp receives (or pays) real Binance funding; the spot leg pays no funding. Spot data is Binance spot 1h, fixed for the 2025 microsecond-timestamp change and resampled to 8h. Delta-neutral; the only P&L besides funding and costs is basis mark-to-market.
candidates.failed_rules: P4 (only 16 out-of-sample entries, below the 20 required; in-sample 42 is fine)
candidates.notes: Leverage: 1x spot notional, which needs about 1.2-1.35x capital once the perp short's margin is counted. The high Sharpe comes from very low volatility, not big profits: out-of-sample CAGR is only 4.1% (2024 +11.0%, 2025 +0.8%, 2026 YTD -0.1%), about what T-bills pay. Invested 52% of the time in-sample and 29% out-of-sample. Neighbours' out-of-sample Sharpe: theta 5 7.27, theta 20 4.83, L3 5.81. Descriptive venue check, same fixed rule, Binance prices as a stand-in for the basis: with Hyperliquid hourly funding the result for 2023-06..2026-09 was +49.8% (CAGR 12.9%) against +15.0% on Binance funding; per year 2023 +11.5%, 2024 +25.7%, 2025 +5.7%, 2026 +1.2%. Running it on Hyperliquid needs its spot markets (UBTC/UETH/USOL); their fees, spreads and minimum sizes were not modelled. In-sample choice was the centre of a flat plateau (all 12 cells had in-sample Sharpe 3.8-8.0).

candidates.name: rel_crowding
candidates.coins: BTC, ETH, SOL (the live desk, equal-weight three $50 accounts)
candidates.params: q=0.90, mode=replace (the relative gate replaces the absolute crowding gate), trailing window 365 days (min 180)
candidates.rules: Uses the desk's own engine (desk.backtest.run) with live per-coin parameters. Only the crowding gate changes. At each 2h close the desk's funding_apr indicator (trailing 3-day mean funding, annualised) is compared with the 90th and 10th percentiles of its own values over the previous 365 days (bars before the current one only; at least 180 days of history). A long entry is blocked when funding_apr is above the 90th percentile. A short entry (ETH breakdown shorts) is blocked when it is below the 10th percentile. The absolute gate (max_crowding 0.85, i.e. longs blocked when 3-day funding is above about 52% APR) is removed. Everything else is unchanged: the hard |funding| <= 150% APR gate, breakout/EMA rules, ATR stops and trail, risk sizing, brakes, costs and funding. It is applied by monkeypatching at runtime; the repo is not edited.
candidates.failed_rules: none as written. Correlation with the desk is 0.95, so P8 is met only through the blend test (0.875 vs 0.852).
candidates.notes: Sizing: the desk's own (BTC 5% risk, ETH/SOL 2%, max 5x). This is a change to the desk, not a new strategy, so the real test is against the stock desk out-of-sample. Sharpe 0.878 vs 0.852, return 45.2% vs 46.2%, max drawdown 13.3% vs 14.7%: within noise. By coin, out-of-sample Sharpe: BTC 0.65 vs 0.87 (worse), ETH 0.84 vs 0.52, SOL 0.41 vs 0.24. The in-sample gain of +0.15 Sharpe shrank to +0.03. Neighbours q=0.80 and q=0.95 scored out-of-sample Sharpe 0.92 and 1.02. Conclusion: it is harmless and possibly a little helpful for ETH/SOL. Choosing it per coin would be tuning on out-of-sample results and would not be validated.

negative_results: (b) Funding z-score contrarian timing for BTC/ETH/SOL, short-only on z > 1.5/2.0/2.5, held 1d/3d/7d, funding lookback 1d or 3d (18 variants, 8h bars, 3-coin book): in-sample Sharpe from -0.74 to +0.39, 15 of 18 negative. Rejected; no out-of-sample run.

observations: Harness bug affecting every hunter: H.spot() timestamps break from 2025-01, when Binance spot zips switched to microseconds, and the index runs to the year 58718. Anything using H.spot after 2024 is wrong. Fixed loader: fb.spot_1h() in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c67283e4-8e62-5bce-a0e4-e537e0ac564b/scratchpad/edge/hunters/funding_basis/fb.py.

Hyperliquid funding is systematically HIGHER than Binance's. From 2023-05-13 to 2026-09-30, mean APR: BTC 14.0% vs 7.2%, ETH 14.1% vs 7.3%, SOL 12.1% vs 4.9%. Hyperliquid was higher on 69-78% of days; daily correlation 0.70-0.76. 42-52% of Hyperliquid hours print exactly the 0.00125%/h baseline (10.95% APR). BTC by year (Hyperliquid vs Binance): 2023 13.9 vs 8.2, 2024 24.1 vs 11.9, 2025 10.6 vs 5.1, 2026 YTD 5.1 vs 2.9. Data: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c67283e4-8e62-5bce-a0e4-e537e0ac564b/scratchpad/edge/hunters/funding_basis/data_hl/. Backtests on Binance funding understate the desk's long carry cost on Hyperliquid and understate carry income for shorts.

Funding the current desk pays (desk engine, live params, 2020-26): BTC $68.7 funding vs $84.6 fees on $890.9 gross trade P&L (7.7%); ETH 9.3% of gross; SOL 7.4%. BTC trades average 1.8x leverage and 2.55 days, about 84 leverage-days a year, so funding costs roughly 3.6% of equity a year. At Hyperliquid's higher rates that becomes roughly +1.2%/yr more for BTC, +0.5% ETH, +0.16% SOL. The 12%/yr drag of buying and holding the BTC perp does not apply, because the desk is flat about 88% of the time. Funding is not why BTC is down in 2026: BTC funding paid in 2026 is 0.23% of equity, against gross trade P&L of -7.7%.
The desk's crowding gate blocks a long only when 3-day average funding is above about 52% APR (0.5+0.5*tanh(apr/60) > 0.85). That is rare outside 2021, which is why the threshold sweep is flat.

Funding and premium extremes on BTC/ETH/SOL carry no contrarian signal. Moderately elevated funding goes with continued uptrends, which supports the desk's trend approach rather than fading crowded funding. Extreme negative funding marks crashes that keep going, so 'buy when shorts pay' would have lost money.

Cross-sectional carry is a separate, market-neutral return source: correlation with the desk -0.01, with BTC -0.08 in-sample / -0.18 out-of-sample, beta to the equal-weight universe -0.01/-0.04. That low correlation is why a 50/50 blend lifts out-of-sample Sharpe from 0.85 to 1.28. It is the most promising item here, but it should be paper-traded with a position cap or stop on the long leg, because the survivorship-biased backtest leaves out collapsing coins with negative funding (LUNA, FTT). It also needs about $100-200 or more per account to meet Hyperliquid's $10 minimum order with 6 legs.

Hyperliquid's funding cross-section (which coins pay most and least) was not tested; only Binance's. Before trading cross-sectional carry on Hyperliquid, download its funding for all 25 coins, check that the ranking matches Binance's, and confirm all 25 are listed there.

Trial accounting: 109 variants in total ((a) 48+1+1, (b) 18, (c) 18, (a2) 12, (d) 11), 3 finalists, each run on 2024-26 once. result.family: Short-horizon mean reversion and volatility regimes (1h-4h bars; vol targeting on 1d bars)
result.summary:
I ran 562 in-sample (2020-23) evaluations across five sub-families and took 3 finalists to out-of-sample (2024-01 to 2026-09) once each. Every in-sample grid run cut the data off at 2024-01-01 first, so no later bar could influence a choice. All results use taker costs (7.5 bps per side) plus real funding, on a BTC/ETH/SOL book with each coin as a 1/3 sleeve.

Mean reversion does not survive out of sample:
(a) Buying 1h crash bounces (a bar down more than 4 sigma, held 3h, long only) had real bounces in-sample: the next 3h averaged +37/+56/+165 bps for BTC/ETH/SOL, IS Sharpe 1.07, near-zero correlation with the desk. Out of sample it fell to Sharpe -0.93 (-21%) and all 8 neighbouring settings lost money. FAIL.
(b) Buying a 4h close near the bar's low (IBS<0.2) inside the desk's uptrend regime had IS Sharpe 1.58. Out of sample: Sharpe -0.07 (-6%), and -49% at 2x costs. FAIL. With maker fills it would have made +52% (Sharpe 1.06), but limit orders placed to buy dips tend to fill on the worst ones, so treat that as optimistic.
(c) Bollinger range trading while the desk's trend filter says no trend: all 72 variants lost money in-sample, even before reaching OOS.
(d) Volatility-squeeze breakouts looked good on BTC/ETH/SOL (IS Sharpe 1.61) but weak on a wider 12-coin basket (0.38), so not taken out of sample.

One strategy passed every rule. Volatility targeting (e) with a trend gate, 'voltgt': hold each coin long only while its daily close is above its 50-day average. Size it at min(2, 40% / 10-day realised vol), skip rebalances smaller than 25%, and scale the whole book by 0.65.
- In-sample: Sharpe 1.80.
- Out-of-sample: Sharpe 0.90, +63.6%, max drawdown 22%, 85 entries.
- At 2x costs out of sample: +58%.
- All 26 neighbouring settings made money out of sample (median Sharpe 0.69).
- Correlation with the desk: 0.50 over the full period, 0.60 out of sample. A 50/50 blend scores Sharpe 0.98 out of sample vs the desk's 0.85.
- Years: +18% in 2024, +18% in 2025, +18% so far in 2026 (vs about -11% for the desk's BTC strategy this year). It lost 18% in 2022.

Caveats:
- It is a slow trend-follower, not a chop strategy, so it will lose alongside the desk in a sustained bear market.
- Most of the edge is the 50-day gate, not the vol targeting (in-sample Sharpe 1.71 without vol targeting vs 1.80 with it). For context, out of sample: buy-and-hold of the three coins scored 0.46 and ungated vol targeting 0.61.
- The three coins were picked in 2026, so survivorship bias applies.
- Out-of-sample correlation sits exactly at the 0.6 limit.

candidates.name: voltgt
candidates.rules: Data: Binance USDT-M perp 1d bars (UTC, resampled from 1h, harness timing), BTC/ETH/SOL; each coin is a 1/3 sleeve of equity. Signal at each daily close t: rv_t = std(last 10 daily close-to-close returns) * sqrt(365); target_t = min(2.0, 0.40 / rv_t) if close_t > SMA50(close)_t, else 0. No-trade band: change the held exposure to target only if target==0, current==0, or |target - current| > 0.25 * current. Sleeve exposure = 0.65 * current / 3 (book max 1.3x notional, typical ~0.4-0.6x). Filled at the next daily open; long only; no stops. Costs 4.5 bps fee + 3 bps slippage per side on every change in exposure, plus real Binance funding.
candidates.coins: BTC, ETH, SOL (equal 1/3 sleeves)
candidates.params: L=10d vol lookback, tv=40%/yr, cap 2.0 per sleeve, band=0.25, gate close>SMA50d, book leverage 0.65
candidates.failed_rules: none (P1-P8 all pass; P8 passes both ways: full-period corr 0.50 and blend 0.978 > 0.852, but the OOS-only corr is 0.599, right at the limit)
candidates.notes: Per year: 2020 +40.3%, 2021 +68.5%, 2022 -17.7%, 2023 +79.9%, 2024 +18.0%, 2025 +17.6%, 2026 to Sep +17.9%. Full-period Sharpe 1.37, max DD 26.5%. OOS funding paid 7.2%, costs 3.5%. Maker side note: OOS Sharpe 0.94. OOS Sharpe by coin at lev 1: BTC 0.89, ETH 1.06, SOL 0.35. As one account per coin at lev 0.65, OOS: BTC Sharpe 0.89 (DD 21%), ETH 1.06 (DD 27%), SOL 0.35 (DD 32%). Blended 50/50 with that coin's desk account, OOS: BTC 0.874->0.995, ETH 0.521->0.902, SOL 0.242->0.347. Context: buy-and-hold of the 3 coins scored OOS Sharpe 0.46 (DD 64% at 1x); ungated vol targeting 0.61 (DD 40%). Most of the edge comes from the SMA50 gate: in-sample, a constant-exposure version scored 1.71 vs 1.80. It is a slow trend-follower, so it overlaps with the desk in direction. The 3 coins were picked in 2026 (survivorship bias). With a $50 account, positions are about $15-40, so the 25% band will often produce rebalance orders below Hyperliquid's $10 minimum; widen the band or skip trades under $10.

candidates.name: crashfade
candidates.rules: Data: Binance perp 1h bars, BTC/ETH/SOL, each coin a 1/3 sleeve. r_t = close_t/close_{t-1}-1; sigma_t = std(r) over the prior 168 bars (t-168..t-1, min 84). If r_t < -4*sigma_t at the close of bar t, go long that coin at exposure 1/3 of equity: fill at the open of t+1, hold 3 bars, exit at the open of t+4 (a new trigger restarts the clock). Long only, no stop, no volume filter (4-sigma bars almost always already have 2x volume). Taker costs plus funding.
candidates.coins: BTC, ETH, SOL (equal 1/3 sleeves)
candidates.params: k=4 sigma, hold n=3 bars, 7-day sigma lookback, long only, leverage 1.0 (1/3x notional per triggered coin)
candidates.notes: In-sample the bounce was real: on the 12-coin basket IS Sharpe 0.89; the next 3h averaged +37/+56/+165 bps for BTC/ETH/SOL. Out of sample it reversed: 2024 -16.6%, 2025 -4.9%, 2026 -0.4%. OOS Sharpe by coin: BTC -1.10, ETH -1.56, SOL +0.24. Still -11% with maker fills.

candidates.name: ibsdip
candidates.rules: Data: Binance perp 4h bars, BTC/ETH/SOL, each coin a 1/3 sleeve. IBS_t = (close-low)/(high-low). Uptrend = EMA50 > EMA200 of 4h closes (same time scale as the desk's EMA100/400 on 2h). Enter long at the close of bar t if IBS_t < 0.2 and uptrend; stay long until the first close with IBS > 0.5 (regime checked only at entry). Fill at the next open; exposure 1/3 per active coin; long only, no stop. Taker costs plus funding.
candidates.coins: BTC, ETH, SOL (equal 1/3 sleeves)
candidates.params: IBS entry < 0.2, exit IBS > 0.5, regime EMA50>EMA200 (4h), leverage 1.0
candidates.failed_rules: P2, P5, P6 (P6 has only 2 pre-declared neighbours, so it is thin anyway)
candidates.notes: Most of the in-sample result came from 2021 (+188%). Costs ate 60% of equity out of sample (86% in-sample). With maker fills (1.5 bps, no slippage) the out-of-sample result would be +52% / Sharpe 1.06, but this is not the main result and is optimistic, because limit orders that buy dips fill on the dips that keep falling. OOS Sharpe by coin: BTC -0.52, ETH +0.25, SOL -0.02.

negative_results: A crashfade (1h, 4-sigma drop, long 3 bars): IS Sharpe 1.07 -> OOS -0.93 (-21%); 0/8 neighbours positive OOS. The in-sample bounce went away in 2024-26.
A, smaller shocks (k=2-3): no edge after costs, e.g. 1h k=2 n=3 long: IS Sharpe 0.54 but -47% at 2x costs in-sample; 1h k=3 n=1: IS 0.55, 2x-cost IS -15%.
A, also fading up-shocks (long/short): worse than long only (1h k=4 n=1 flow filter: 0.53 vs 1.01 long only); shorting after pumps loses.
A, volume (2x median) and taker-flow (<45% buy share) filters: no gain; 4-sigma bars almost always already carry 2x volume (k=4 n=3: off 1.065, vol 1.049, flow 0.825 IS).
B ibsdip (4h IBS<0.2 in desk uptrend): IS 1.58 -> OOS -0.07 (-6.1%), 2x-cost OOS -48.6%, 0/2 neighbours positive.

B, RSI(2) dips: only the 1h th=5 ex=70 uptrend version was good in-sample (1.43, 2x-cost IS Sharpe 0.45; not taken OOS because it is the same idea as ibsdip with a lower IS Sharpe). The 2h/4h RSI2 versions scored <= 0.69 IS; the 'any' and 'flat' regimes were much worse (e.g. 1h th5 ex70 any 0.85, 2h th10 ex50 any 0.35).
B, IBS/RSI dips in the 'flat' (no-trend) regime: IS Sharpe <= 0.56 and negative at 2x costs. Dip-buying only worked inside uptrends in 2020-23.
B, in-sample edge is partly uptrend beta: simply holding long whenever the desk's 4h uptrend filter is on scored IS Sharpe 1.70 (DD 60%), above ibsdip's 1.58.
C, Bollinger range trading only while EMA100/400 are within 1/2/4% or ER(48)<0.3: all 72 variants lost money in-sample (best 4h N50 m1.5 g<1%: Sharpe -0.13; typical -0.4 to -0.8).
D, volatility-squeeze breakout (2h BB-width pct<20% + 20-bar high + desk trend filter + 3-ATR chandelier): IS 1.61 on BTC/ETH/SOL but only 0.38 on the 12-coin basket; not taken OOS.
D, NR7 squeeze breakout: IS up to 1.59 (2h, desk trend, chandelier) with the same weak-basket concern; trend-like (IS corr 0.42 with desk); not taken OOS.

D-complement, squeeze gate on a desk-style 60-bar breakout (approximate desk model): IS Sharpe 1.30 -> 1.65 (q=0.2, last 12 bars), 202 -> 108 entries; 26/26 IS neighbours positive (median 1.50); 12-coin basket 0.61. Not taken OOS: an IS-only lead, unvalidated.
E, ungated vol-targeted long: IS Sharpe 1.1-1.3 with DD ~60% at lev 1; OOS context 0.61 (DD 40%), below the gated version.
E, vol-targeting adds little to the SMA50 gate: in-sample, constant exposure with the same gate scored 1.71 vs 1.80; SMA100 gates scored 1.33-1.41.
observations: The 4-sigma 1h crash bounce in BTC/ETH/SOL was large and consistent in 2020-23 (+37/+56/+165 bps average over the next 3h) but did not hold up 2024-26 (strategy -17% in 2024, -5% in 2025). Do not build a liquidation-bounce bot on 2020-23 evidence.

Strategies that hold 1-4h are dominated by costs at 15 bps per round trip. ibsdip paid costs equal to 60% of equity out of sample, and its sign flips between taker (-6%) and maker (+52%) assumptions. Any short-horizon idea for the desk depends on getting maker fills, which brings adverse-selection risk the backtest cannot see.
Bollinger range trading in the desk's 'no trend' state lost money in every one of 72 variants in-sample, so 1-4h crypto bars show no band reversion to harvest while the desk is flat.

The one robust thing found is slow: daily close above SMA50, sized to a 40% vol target (voltgt). Out of sample it scored Sharpe 0.90, DD 22%, +18% in each of 2024, 2025 and 2026 YTD. It works best on ETH (OOS Sharpe 1.06; ETH desk account 0.52 -> 0.90 blended 50/50) and BTC (0.89; BTC account 0.87 -> 0.995 blended); on SOL it is weak (0.35).

For context, buy-and-hold of the three coins scored OOS Sharpe 0.46 with DD 64% at 1x. The SMA50 gate is what adds value, roughly doubling Sharpe and cutting drawdown by about two-thirds; vol targeting alone (ungated) scored only 0.61.

voltgt is in the market about 63% of the time vs the desk's mostly-flat profile, but it is still long-only trend: correlation with the desk is 0.50 over the full period and 0.60 out of sample, and it lost 18% in 2022. It diversifies the desk's timing, not its direction.

Untested lead for the desk team: requiring a Bollinger-width squeeze (below the 20th percentile of the last 90 days, within the last 12 bars) before the 60-bar breakout raised a desk-approximation's IS Sharpe from 1.30 to 1.65 while halving trades. This is a new kind of gate (compression), unlike the rejected strength/efficiency/extension gates, but it has not been tested out of sample. It needs a pre-registered test in the real desk backtest (intrabar stops, risk sizing) before anyone believes it.

Practical constraint: at $50 per account, voltgt positions are about $15-40 notional, so its 25% rebalance band often produces orders under Hyperliquid's $10 minimum. Live, it should rebalance only on gate flips or changes of $10 or more.
Survivorship: BTC/ETH/SOL (and the 12-coin check basket) were chosen in 2026; SOL in particular is a known winner, which flatters any long-only result.

It also survives one extra bar of delay (OOS 0.52) and any daily-bar start hour (0.51-0.84). Even so, it does not hold up as an edge for this desk. The whole OOS result is November 2024: without that month OOS is -6.1% (Sharpe -0.09), and the 53-neighbour family's median falls to -0.18 with only 25% positive. candidate.rules: Data: Binance USDT-M perp daily candles (00:00 UTC bars, H.klines(c,'1d')), real funding. Universe: BTC ETH SOL BNB XRP DOGE ADA AVAX LINK DOT LTC BCH TRX ATOM NEAR UNI AAVE FIL ETC XLM (a coin trades once its indicators are warm). Signal at each daily close t, per coin: s = mean over L in {7,14,28,56,112} days of sign(close_t/close_{t-L} - 1); long-only, so s is clipped at 0. sigma_ann = std of the last 40 daily returns x sqrt(365). Raw weight = s x 0.40 / sigma_ann / N_eligible. Portfolio scaler k_t = 0.30 / (std of the raw portfolio's last 60 daily returns (raw weights at t-1 x returns at t) x sqrt(365)), clipped to [0,4]; target = raw x k; total gross capped at 3x by proportional scaling. No-trade band: a coin's held weight changes only if |target - held| > 0.2 x |target|, or the sign changes, or target or held is 0. Timing: decide at daily close t, fill at open t+1 (harness backtest_portfolio); 7.5 bps per side on |delta weight|; funding paid on held weight. No stops, no take-profit; exits happen when the signal goes to 0.

votes.summary:
I could not refute tsmom20_long, but I can't confirm it either.

**What holds up:**
- The code is clean: a truncation test found no look-ahead, and costs and funding are applied on every leg.
- Selection used in-sample data only, with 3 finalists, and the re-run reproduces every claimed number exactly.
- It survives 2x and 3x costs, an extra day of delay (OOS Sharpe 0.68), different daily-bar anchor hours (0.63-0.86) and the 26-neighbour grid.
- A real survivorship test does not explain the result. On all 69 Binance perps listed by Oct 2020, including 24 later delisted, OOS Sharpe is 0.78; the 49 non-survivors alone get 0.64.

**What I can't confirm:**
- Out-of-sample alpha over simply being long crypto is not statistically significant: t ≈ 1.0-1.25 against BTC, the equal-weight index and a passive vol-targeted long book.
- The OOS profit comes from three bursts (March 2024, November 2024 and 21 Aug 2026). The top 5 days are 80% of the OOS log-return, and from Dec 2024 to Jul 2026 it lost 14%.
- The 30% vol target does not hold. After quiet periods the scaler caps at 4x, and on 21 Aug 2026 the book ran at 2.6x gross and about 81% ex-ante vol.
- P7 passes only at the base case (34.0% vs 35%). The drawdown breaches 35% with +1 day delay (38%), 2x costs (36.6%), three of five other bar anchors, and the point-in-time universe.
- In-sample deflated Sharpe over the 97 trials is 0.76.

My own pre-declared rule puts it at UNCERTAIN: the mechanics survive, but the edge can't be told apart from beta plus a few lucky days. Of everything I tested, dropping the best 5 days came closest to breaking it (0.94 to 0.32), but the desk fails that test even harder.

It is likely a genuine but modest crypto trend premium, and diversifying for the desk (correlation 0.49). It is not executable on the $150 accounts ($10 minimum orders, roughly $4 median positions) and needs about $2-5k. If it is ever used, the scaler cap should be lowered, and that change would have to be pre-registered and tested in-sample only.

The increment over the stock desk, which is the actual claim, is zero:
- Only 54 of 1004 OOS days have a different desk return at all.
- Mean daily difference is -0.43%/yr (t = -0.13). OOS return is lower: 45.2% vs 46.2%.
- The +0.027 Sharpe comes from lower volatility (30 fewer trades), not from more return.
- Block-bootstrap Sharpe difference OOS: +0.027, SE 0.22, 90% CI [-0.38, +0.32], P(diff <= 0) = 0.40.

issues: No look-ahead found. The trailing quantile is s.shift(1).rolling(4380 bars, min 2160), so it uses past bars only. funding_apr counts prints with bar.ts < ts <= bar close, which are published by the decision time; the stock desk uses the same rule. The engine decides at the bar close and fills at the next open, and stops are checked against bar high/low. Every run reverts the patch afterwards (install(None)), so it does not leak into the stock run. The stock run reproduces the stated desk numbers (IS 1.515 / OOS 0.852). cost_mult really reaches the broker: fees rise with the multiplier. Funding is charged on every bar a position is held, in both variants.

Selection discipline is clean for this candidate. The 11-variant overlay grid was run on IS only (d_overlay.py with end=IS_END; d_overlay_is.csv written at 21:34, before the finals at 21:38). The neighbours q=0.80 and q=0.95 were declared in advance. 3 finalists were reported, and nothing was re-selected after the OOS run.

MAIN FLAW, which explains the PASS: the candidate is the stock desk with a gate tweak. Daily correlation is 0.95 and the daily returns are identical on 95% of OOS days. P2-P7 are passed by the desk's own performance, not by the overlay. P8 is met only through the 50/50 blend clause, and for a near-clone of the desk that clause reduces to 'Sharpe slightly above the desk's', which here is a coin flip (bootstrap P(diff <= 0) = 0.40). The pass rule was written for a new strategy; for a change to the desk the right test is the improvement, and the improvement is statistically zero.

The OOS improvement in returns is slightly negative: mean daily difference -0.43%/yr, t = -0.13. The 'diff Sharpe' (Sharpe of the daily return difference) is -0.08, with a probabilistic Sharpe of 0.45 that it is above zero.

The IS improvement (+0.153 Sharpe) is the best of 11 IS variants. It is not significant even before deflation: bootstrap SE 0.116, one-sided p = 0.066, probabilistic Sharpe 0.88. Deflated Sharpe of the improvement series: 0.66 counting the 11 overlay variants, 0.48 counting the hunter's 109 total trials.

Simpler variants from the same IS grid score as well or better OOS (descriptive only; this is not a basis for picking one). Absolute threshold 0.75 gives OOS 0.931 and 0.80 gives 0.899, versus 0.878 for the chosen relative gate. The 11 variants span OOS Sharpe 0.795-1.022 and the chosen one sits in the middle. The relative-quantile idea is not distinguishable from simply tightening the existing threshold. Note also that the 'add' and 'replace' modes give identical OOS results: the absolute gate never binds once the relative gate is present.

Results hinge on a handful of trades. BTC's OOS shortfall (2024: +69% stock vs +27%) comes mainly from one blocked winner (entry 2024-02-26, +$238, +23% on notional). ETH's gain comes from 16 blocked trades (7 shorts, 9 longs, net -$16.6). Removing the 5 days where the relative gate most beat the stock desk reverses the ranking: Sharpe 0.90 vs 1.05.

Minor: in replace mode there is no crowding gate at all until each coin has 180 days of history (SOL until 2021-03, BTC/ETH through mid-2020). Before that the variant runs ungated. This is in-sample, and it is the source of the extra SOL trades in early 2021.

The ETH improvement shows up in both periods (IS +0.31, OOS +0.32 Sharpe; bootstrap 90% CI [0.16, 0.58]). Picking it per coin now would be tuning on OOS results, as the hunter says. It is a lead to pre-register and test on new data, not a validated edge.

candidate.rules: Data: Binance USDT-M perp 1d bars (UTC, resampled from 1h, harness timing), BTC/ETH/SOL; each coin is a 1/3 sleeve of equity. Signal at each daily close t: rv_t = std(last 10 daily close-to-close returns) * sqrt(365); target_t = min(2.0, 0.40 / rv_t) if close_t > SMA50(close)_t, else 0. No-trade band: change the held exposure to target only if target==0, current==0, or |target - current| > 0.25 * current. Sleeve exposure = 0.65 * current / 3 (book max 1.3x notional, typical ~0.4-0.6x). Filled at the next daily open; long only; no stops. Costs 4.5 bps fee + 3 bps slippage per side on every change in exposure, plus real Binance funding.

candidate.rules: Data: Binance daily perp bars (00:00 UTC). Funding per day = sum of prints in (open, close] (H.bar_funding '1d'), known at the close. Signal = rolling 7-day mean of the daily funding sums. Eligible coins that day: at least 60 days since the first funding print, a close that day, and a signal value; at least 6 eligible coins needed. At each daily close: short the 3 highest-signal coins at -0.5/3 each and long the 3 lowest at +0.5/3 each, then multiply all weights by 0.6, so gross 0.6x and each leg 0.1x of equity. Fill at the next open and hold one day. Rebalance daily. Costs: 7.5 bps per side on each weight change only (unchanged legs cost nothing; no drift rebalancing charged). Real Binance funding is paid or received on each leg. No stops. Market-neutral: beta to the equal-weight universe is -0.01 in-sample and -0.04 out-of-sample.

It does not beat cash. The Sharpe is not measured against a risk-free rate. Out-of-sample CAGR is 4.13% against roughly 4.28% for 3-month T-bills over the same years. Those T-bill yields are approximate annual averages from memory, and 2026 is an estimate. Measured against T-bills, the out-of-sample Sharpe is -0.41.

The P8 blend benefit is what holding cash would give. A 50/50 desk plus T-bill mix scores an out-of-sample Sharpe of 1.089, against 1.076 for desk plus this strategy. In 2025-05 to 2026-09 it is 1.102 for T-bills against 0.924. Any steady, low-volatility positive return passes the blend test.

The Sharpe is inflated by autocorrelation. Daily returns are 0.5-0.7 correlated with the previous 1-5 days, because funding regimes persist. Correcting for that (Lo's method, 10 lags) gives Sharpe 3.16 in-sample, 2.49 out-of-sample and 0.75 for the second half.

It needs more capital than the returns assume. Spot equal to 100% of equity plus margin for the perp short means about 1.2x equity at 5x perp leverage. Out-of-sample CAGR per unit of real capital is about 3.4%.

Risks the backtest leaves out: liquidation or margin top-ups on the perp short during a sharp rally (spot and perp margin are assumed to move freely), the spread on Hyperliquid spot, and exchange counterparty risk.
Trial count: the 12 in the claim covers only this family. The hunter's whole study ran 109 variants, which matters for the noise bar below.

The hunter's neighbour check only had 3 cells, and its 'theta' changes the entry and exit thresholds together. My 6 pre-declared neighbours also pass: median out-of-sample Sharpe 6.0, 6 of 6 positive.

votes.summary:
The backtest reproduces almost exactly, and the funding income it earns is genuine. Shorting the perp while holding spot did collect funding on 20 of 20 coins from 2020 to April 2025, with almost no basis loss.

As an edge for the desk, though, it doesn't hold up:
- **It already misses the pass rule:** 16 out-of-sample entries, 20 required.
- **It has stopped working:** in the most recent 17 months it made +0.25% on BTC/ETH/SOL, and about 0% on each of 17 other coins. That half's Sharpe of 1.09 is below the noise bar of about 2.6.
- **It doesn't beat cash:** out-of-sample CAGR of 4.1% is about the T-bill rate, so its Sharpe over T-bills is -0.41. Its improvement to the desk blend matches a 50/50 desk plus T-bill mix (1.076 against 1.089).
- **The Sharpe is overstated:** daily returns are strongly autocorrelated; corrected, the out-of-sample Sharpe is about 2.5, not 6.8.
- **On Hyperliquid itself** it made only about 1.9-2.3% over the last 13 months.

Verdict UNCERTAIN, leaning against deploying it as an edge. At best it is a way to earn something like a cash yield on idle USDC when funding sits at or above its default 10.95% APR. It needs about 1.2x capital and carries execution risks the backtest leaves out (perp short margin, Hyperliquid spot spreads).

result.summary:
I evaluated about 800 in-sample cells: 408 event-study cells, 24 momentum-control cells, 14 lag variants, and 330 costed backtest configs plus 26 desk-filter cells. I took 3 finalists to out-of-sample, once each.

One rule passes P1-P8: C1_ls_4h, a contrarian trade on the Binance all-account long/short ratio (count_long_short_ratio, the "retail" ratio). It runs on 4h bars. Take the log of the ratio and its z-score against the last 90 days. If z < -1.5, go long 1x; if z > 1.5, go short 1x. Hold each signal 24h; a new signal restarts the hold.
- Sizing: one account per coin (BTC, ETH, SOL) at 1x when signalled, blended equal-weight.
- In-sample (2020-09 to 2023): Sharpe 2.08, +686%, max drawdown 15%, 267 entries.
- Out-of-sample: Sharpe 0.96, +78.5%, max drawdown 29.6%, 292 entries. At 2x costs it still makes +54%.
- Neighbours: all 6 are positive out-of-sample, median Sharpe 0.66.
- Correlation with the desk is 0.21. A 50/50 blend has an out-of-sample Sharpe of 1.11, against 0.85 for the desk alone.
- It is not a timestamp leak: adding 65 or 245 minutes of data lag still gives out-of-sample Sharpe 0.98 / 0.80. It is not disguised momentum either: price momentum has a negative IC in-sample, and the signal gets stronger after controlling for price.

Caveats that matter:
- The out-of-sample Sharpe is half the in-sample one.
- Profit is concentrated: the top 10 of 292 out-of-sample trades make all the net profit, and the win rate is 38%.
- 2026 so far is flat (-0.1%).
- The long-only version FAILED (out-of-sample Sharpe 0.39). Out-of-sample, the short side carried more (Sharpe 0.93 vs 0.39 for longs).
- As separate $50 accounts at 1x, ETH would have drawn down 54% and SOL 42% out-of-sample. Only the 3-coin blend stays under 35%.

Everything else failed:
- Taker-flow imbalance: dead after costs (best in-sample Sharpe 0.53 of 144 configs).
- OI-confirmed "new longs" (price up with OI up): in-sample 1.30, out-of-sample -0.06. FAIL.
- OI flush / capitulation bounce: no in-sample edge.
- Top-trader signals: their sign flips from year to year.
- OI rising into desk breakouts: no predictive value, and the sign flips by coin.
- An order-flow entry filter on the desk: in-sample gain of 1.51 to 1.64 but it hurt SOL. Not robust, not taken.

candidates.name: C1_ls_4h
candidates.coins: BTC, ETH, SOL (one account each, equal-weight blend)
candidates.rules: Data: Binance USDT-M perp 4h klines (H.klines) plus H.metrics(coin) column count_long_short_ratio (global ACCOUNT long/short ratio). For each 4h bar with open time t, take the last 5-min metrics row stamped <= t+4h-5min (5-min safety lag; zeros = NaN; a row older than 1h = NaN). R = log(ratio). z = (R - rolling mean)/rolling std over 540 bars (90 days, min 180 bars). Event at bar close: z < -1.5 -> long (+1); z > 1.5 -> short (-1); otherwise none. Position = latest event held for 6 bars (24h), re-armed by every new event; an opposite event flips at once; with no event in the last 6 bars, flat. Decide at bar close, fill at next bar open (harness timing). Costs 4.5 bps fee + 3 bps slippage per side on |dpos|, real Binance funding. Sizing: each coin account 1.0x notional when signalled; desk = equal-weight average of the 3 accounts (portfolio weight 1/3 per coin, gross <= 1x). No stops. ETH/SOL metrics only exist from 2021-12, so they are flat before then.
candidates.params: interval=4h, W=90d, k=1.5, H=6 bars, side=long/short, lag=5min, 1x per coin account (1/3 portfolio weight)
candidates.failed_rules: none
candidates.notes: Passes all of P1-P8 as written. Neighbour OOS Sharpes: W30 0.66, W180 0.95, k1.0 0.62, k2.0 0.66, H1 0.42, H12 0.91. Per year: 2020 +4.8%, 2021 +33%, 2022 +196%, 2023 +90%, 2024 +27.8%, 2025 +39.8%, 2026 -0.1%. Post-hoc diagnostics (not used for selection): per-coin OOS Sharpe BTC 1.16 (DD 24%), ETH 0.56 (DD 54% at 1x), SOL 0.54 (DD 42% at 1x), so separate $50 accounts at 1x would breach 35% on ETH/SOL; per-account sizing would need roughly 0.5x on ETH/SOL. OOS: long side Sharpe 0.39, short side 0.93. 292 OOS trades, win rate 38%; the top 10 trades equal all the net profit. Robust to extra data lag (+65 min: OOS Sharpe 0.98; +245 min: 0.80). In-sample it received about 15% of equity in funding; OOS about 0, so the OOS edge is price-driven. A live version needs Binance's public globalLongShortAccountRatio (5m) endpoint at each 4h close while trading on Hyperliquid, whose funding differs. In-sample the whole 72-config grid was positive (min Sharpe 0.72), which lowers but does not remove selection bias. Metrics in-sample is 2020-09..2023 for BTC and 2021-12..2023 for ETH/SOL only.

candidates.coins: BTC, ETH, SOL (one account each, equal-weight blend)
candidates.rules: 2h bars. dOI = 6-bar change of log(sum_open_interest), from the last metrics row stamped <= bar close - 5min; z vs rolling 1080 bars (90d). Long 1x when z(dOI) > 1.5 AND the 6-bar log price change > 0 ('new longs'); hold 3 bars (6h), re-armed. Harness timing and costs; 1x per coin account, 1/3 portfolio weight.
candidates.params: interval=2h, n=6, k=1.5, H=3, long-only
candidates.notes: 48% of the in-sample return came from 2023 alone; only 17.6% of the 108-config grid reached in-sample Sharpe 0.7, so this was a weak finalist. OI-confirmed short-term continuation does not survive out of sample.

negative_results: A1 taker order-flow imbalance (net aggressive-buy share over n bars, z vs 90d) as a time-series signal on 12 coins listed by 2020: 144 costed in-sample configs (4h/1d, n 1-12, k 0.5-1.5, hold 1-6, momentum and contrarian). None reaches in-sample Sharpe 0.7 (best 0.53, 1d n3 k1.5 H3 momentum). Dead after costs.

A event study: 1-bar flow is mildly contrarian (rank-IC -0.025 to -0.035, negative in 4/4 years) and 3-6 day flow is mildly momentum (IC ~0.028, 2021 negative). Both are too small to pay 15 bps round trips.
A2 price-residualised flow (absorption): IC ~0.033-0.037 in the momentum direction, not contrarian as hypothesised. Not pursued after the A1 costed results.
B OI flush / capitulation (OI z < -k and price z < -k -> long): no consistent in-sample excess return across 324 event cells; signs vary by year (e.g. 2h n24 H12: -78 bps).

B 'new shorts' (price down + OI up): forward excess return NEGATIVE (e.g. 2h n6 H3 k2: -131 bps). Shorts piling in tends to be followed by more downside, not a squeeze; the long/short follow version topped out at in-sample Sharpe 0.85.
B 'new longs' long-only (finalist F3): in-sample Sharpe 1.30, out-of-sample -0.06 (-3.9%), 2x cost -20.9%, 1/6 neighbours positive. FAIL.
C top-trader position ratio (follow) and top-minus-retail divergence: IC sign flips across years (e.g. 4h W90 H6 top_follow: 2020 -0.24, 2021 +0.02, 2022 -0.43). Inconsistent, not taken.
C1 long-only retail contrarian (finalist F2): in-sample 1.82, out-of-sample 0.39 (+16%). FAIL on P2.

D OI rising into desk breakouts: over 120 in-sample desk long trades with metrics, rank-corr of entry dOI (12/30/60 bars) with trade return is only +0.03 to +0.06 and flips sign by coin (BTC +0.2, SOL -0.15 to -0.35). Skipping falling-OI entries would skip trades averaging +1.3% to +1.9%. No filter value.

D order-flow entry filter on the desk (skip a breakout if 30/60/120-bar flow z <= 0 or <= -0.5): approximate in-sample desk Sharpe 1.51 -> 1.64 for OFI30 but SOL 0.76 -> 0.46; OFI60/120 give no gain or a loss. Not robust, not taken out of sample.
D retail ratio at desk entry: entries with zR > 0 averaged +0.3% vs +2.2% (n=21 vs 99). Too thin to act on; not tested out of sample.
observations: Data fact: H.metrics for ETH and SOL starts 2021-12-01, not 2020-09 (BTC starts 2020-09-01). Metrics-based in-sample work for ETH/SOL covers only 2 years.

Timestamp check: a metrics taker-ratio row stamped T describes the 5 minutes ENDING at T (correlation with 1h kline taker share is best, 0.85, for rows in (h, h+60]), and the OI row at T is a snapshot at T (OI value / OI equals the kline close at T to within 0.7 bp). So 'rows <= bar close' is correct; I used close - 5 min for safety.

The Binance all-account (retail) long/short ratio is the strongest positioning signal found. Contrarian rank-IC is positive in 4/4 in-sample years in every cell tested, 0.04-0.12; it gets stronger after controlling for price, and it is not momentum (price momentum has a negative IC at these horizons in-sample). The edge decays over about a day (a 1-bar 1d lag halves it).
C1_ls_4h is close to uncorrelated with the desk (0.21 daily; 0.35 OOS). A 50/50 blend improves desk OOS Sharpe from 0.85 to 1.11. It is the only result in this family that adds to the desk.

C1 out-of-sample is carried more by its short side (Sharpe 0.93) than its long side (0.39), and by BTC (1.16) more than ETH/SOL (0.56/0.54). As stand-alone $50 accounts at 1x, ETH and SOL would have drawn down 54%/42% out of sample, so per-account sizing would need roughly 0.5x on ETH/SOL. Only the 3-coin blend stays at 29.6%.
C1 is fat-tailed: OOS win rate 38%, and the top 10 of 292 trades equal all the net profit. Like the desk, it was roughly flat to negative in 2026H1 (half-year Sharpe -0.14).

C1 received funding in-sample (about 15% of equity over 2020-23), because the retail-short / negative-funding regimes overlap. Out of sample funding was about 0. On Hyperliquid funding differs, so the in-sample backtest flatters a live version somewhat.
C1 live needs Binance's public 5-min globalLongShortAccountRatio feed read at each 4h close. It tolerates data delay well: +65 min gives OOS Sharpe 0.98 and +245 min gives 0.80.

Taker-buy share has structural per-coin levels (in-sample mean 0.48-0.50) and is strongly contemporaneous with price. Raw order flow carries almost no tradeable forward information after 7.5 bps per side.

The 25-coin universe is survivorship-biased. The order-flow tests used only the 12 coins listed by early 2020, and the metrics tests only BTC/ETH/SOL, which are not survivorship-sensitive at this scale.
I ran the repo's desk backtest read-only (PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, network blocked) to get its trade list (desk_trades.csv in my directory). git status in the repo is clean afterwards.

votes.reproduced:
Exact match. Re-running final_C1_ls_4h.py gives IS Sharpe 2.081, return +686.1%, max DD 15.3%, 267 entries. OOS gives Sharpe 0.963, return +78.5%, DD 29.6%, 292 entries. OOS at 2x costs: +54.3% (Sharpe 0.753). Neighbour OOS Sharpes: W30 0.66, W180 0.95, k1.0 0.62, k2.0 0.66, H1 0.42, H12 0.91, so the median is 0.656 and 6/6 are positive. Correlation with the desk is 0.212; the OOS blend Sharpe is 1.111 vs 0.852 for the desk alone. P1-P8 all hold as written.

I also wrote an independent version: my own signal built with merge_asof and my own open-to-open simulator (vlib.py). Its signals match the hunter's bar for bar on all three coins (0 mismatches) and it gives IS 2.085 / OOS 0.963, DD 29.6%. Costs are charged per coin leg on |change in position| and funding is applied to every leg; both match the harness.
issues: Not significant out-of-sample on its own: OOS t-stat 1.60 (one-sided p 0.055; about 0.17 after correcting for the 3 finalists taken to OOS). A 20-day block bootstrap of OOS Sharpe gives 5th percentile 0.01, median 0.97, 95th percentile 1.90; P(Sharpe <= 0) is 4.8% and P(Sharpe < 0.5) is 21%. Deflated Sharpe on OOS with N=3 finalists is 0.82, below the usual 0.95.

The edge has weakened: Sharpe halved from IS 2.08 to OOS 0.96. 2026 YTD is -0.1% (Sharpe 0.10), and 2025Q1 and 2026Q1 had quarterly Sharpe of about -1.6. The sides swapped between periods: IS long side 1.83 / short 0.81, OOS long 0.39 / short 0.93. The long-only finalist failed P2.

Gains are concentrated in a few days: dropping the best 5 OOS days gives Sharpe 0.44 (below the 0.5 bar, return still +22%), the best 10 gives 0.00, the best 20 gives -0.82. This is typical for crypto and less concentrated than the desk itself (desk drop-5 Sharpe -0.06) or BTC buy and hold (0.37).

Per-account sizing breaches P7: run as three separate $50 accounts at 1x, the OOS max DD is ETH 54% and SOL 42%. P7 holds only for the equal-weight blend (DD 29.6%, which reaches 33% at 3x costs). A deployable version needs about 0.5x on ETH/SOL (OOS DD 31%/23%, Sharpe unchanged at 0.56/0.55). That sizing is set after seeing OOS, but it is pure scaling.

Trial counts don't match: the claim reports 146 IS trials, but PLAN.md logs about 800 cells (408 event-study cells, 72 C1 configs, 144 A1, 108 B, 26 D, and others). IS deflated Sharpe is about 0.98 at N=146 but about 0.80 at N=800. These use cross-trial Sharpe dispersions I assumed (0.35-0.6), so treat them as rough.

The in-sample period is thin: metrics only start 2020-09 for BTC and 2021-12 for ETH/SOL, and 2022-23 supply most of the IS return (+196%, +90%). In-sample the strategy received about 15% of equity in funding, mostly SOL in 2022. OOS funding is about 0.
BTC carries the most weight: leaving out BTC drops OOS Sharpe to 0.70; leaving out ETH or SOL leaves it at 0.96.

Live data needed: going live needs Binance's public globalLongShortAccountRatio (5m) at every 4h close, plus a 90-day history built from the data.binance.vision dump. Robustness to a 245-minute lag means latency is not critical.

Look-ahead checks are clean. No look-ahead found: the metrics row used is stamped <= bar close minus 5 min, the rolling z is causal, and fills happen at the next open. A timestamp test found no forward leak: ratio changes before a price bar correlate at most |0.08| with it, while ratio changes in the hour after a bar correlate -0.17 to -0.30, so the ratio lags price. No data errors: regular 5-min stamps, no zeros, only 3 stale runs on BTC.
Selection looks clean: the IS grid scripts predate the finalist scripts, and each OOS output was written once. Survivorship is not an issue: BTC/ETH/SOL are the desk's fixed coins.

Separate harness bug, not used by this candidate: H.spot() reads Binance spot files from 2025 on, whose open_time is in microseconds, as milliseconds. This produced out-of-range dates and was OOM-killed when resampled. Any hunter using H.spot for OOS work would get broken data. I worked around it in v_spot2.py.
