votes.summary:
I could not refute C1_ls_4h. The code is clean, and the numbers reproduce exactly in both the hunter's script and my independent version, with bar-for-bar identical signals. I found no look-ahead, no missing costs or funding, no selection on OOS and no data errors.

It survives every stress I applied:
- 2x and 3x costs: OOS Sharpe 0.75 and 0.54.
- One extra bar of delay: 0.80.
- Data lag up to 4h: 0.80-0.98.
- All four 4h bar phases: 0.91-1.08.
- Spot-price execution: 0.97.
- No funding: 0.95.
- Market beta about 0.
- A price-only mirror of the rule fails, so the edge comes from the long/short ratio, not disguised momentum.

So it passes P1-P8 as written. But this is a modest, statistically marginal edge, not a strong one. The OOS t-stat is only 1.6, the bootstrap 5th-percentile Sharpe is about 0, and deflated Sharpe with N=3 is 0.82. Sharpe halved from IS to OOS, 2026 YTD is flat, and the long and short sides swapped strength between periods. Dropping the 5 best OOS days takes Sharpe to 0.44, though that's less fragile than the desk itself. As three separate $50 accounts it needs about 0.5x on ETH/SOL to keep drawdown under 35%.

A realistic live expectation is an OOS Sharpe of roughly 0.5-1, market-neutral, and additive to the desk (blend 1.11 vs 0.85). It is worth paper-trading at small size, with the 2026 weakness watched.

Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c67283e4-8e62-5bce-a0e4-e537e0ac564b/scratchpad/edge/verify/positioning_flow_C1_ls_4h_code_p/: vlib.py, v_reproduce.py, v_stress.py, v_phase.py, v_spot2.py, v_mirror.py, v_dsr.py, v_last.py, v_tstamp.py, v_inspect_data.py.

Separately, H.spot() in the shared harness misreads spot data from 2025 on (microsecond timestamps). It doesn't affect this candidate but could break other hunters' work.

votes.reproduced:
My re-implementation, written from the rules text alone with the harness before I opened any hunter script, reproduces the claim almost exactly. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c67283e4-8e62-5bce-a0e4-e537e0ac564b/scratchpad/edge/verify/positioning_flow_C1_ls_4h_independent_p/final_verify_C1_ls_4h.py (helper vlib.py in the same folder, output in out_final_verify.json).
- In-sample: Sharpe 2.08 vs 2.081 claimed, return +686.1% vs +686.1%, max drawdown 15.3% vs 15.3%, entries 266 vs 267.
- Out-of-sample: Sharpe 0.963 vs 0.963, return +78.5% vs +78.5%, max drawdown 29.6% vs 29.6%, entries 292 vs 292.
- Out-of-sample at 2x costs: +54.3% vs +54.3%.
- Correlation with the desk 0.212 vs 0.212; 50/50 blend Sharpe 1.111 vs 1.111 (desk alone 0.852).
- Per year matches: 2020 +4.8%, 2021 +33%, 2022 +196%, 2023 +90%, 2024 +27.8%, 2025 +39.8%, 2026 -0.1%.
- Neighbour grid: W30 0.67, W180 0.95, k1.0 0.59 (hunter 0.62), k2.0 0.65, H1 0.42, H12 0.91. Median about 0.66, 6 of 6 positive, so P6 passes.
- Per coin at 1x, out-of-sample: BTC 1.16 (drawdown 24%), ETH 0.56 (drawdown 54%), SOL 0.54 (drawdown 42%).
- Long side alone 0.39, short side alone 0.93.
Afterwards I read the hunter's code: it matches my reading of the rules. The only small gap is in the k1.0 neighbour (0.59 vs 0.62). It comes from zero-ratio rows: I fall back to the previous non-zero row, they set the value to missing.
Under the pre-registered rule as written, P1-P8 all pass. I confirm the PASS mechanically.
issues: Trial count is understated. The claim reports 146 in-sample trials, but the hunter's own PLAN.md logs about 800 evaluated cells (408 event-study cells used to pick this signal family, 72 cells in the C1 grid, 144 in A1, 108 in B, 26 in D, 24 in C2, 14 lag tests). The deflated-Sharpe hurdle should use the larger number, or at least say so.

The out-of-sample Sharpe of 0.96 does not clear the deflated hurdle sqrt(2 ln N)/sqrt(T) with T = 2.75 years: 1.90 at N=146, 2.21 at N=800. It only just clears the best-of-3-finalists hurdle (0.89). The in-sample Sharpe of 2.08 (T about 3.33 years) clears 1.73 at N=146 and only barely clears 2.00 at N=800.

Generality on the 8 coins the hunter never used (identical rule, Binance metrics I downloaded myself, 2021-12 to 2026-09) is weak. Out-of-sample Sharpe: BNB 0.01, XRP 0.41, DOGE 0.64, ADA 1.09, LINK -0.05, LTC -0.34, AVAX -0.33, DOT 0.30. Only 4 of 8 have a positive return. The equal-weight basket of the 8 is 0.54, but without ADA it drops to 0.23, and without ADA and DOGE to 0.01. In 2022-23 the same basket had a Sharpe of only 0.55, against 2.08 for BTC/ETH/SOL in their in-sample window, so the three selected coins look unusually favourable.

The out-of-sample profit on BTC/ETH/SOL comes from the short leg (Sharpe 0.93). The long leg is 0.39 overall and -0.02 in the second out-of-sample half. On the unselected coins the short leg is negative on 4 of 8 (BNB -0.24, XRP -0.59, LINK -0.36, AVAX -0.80). The leg that carries the result is the one that generalises least.

Profit is concentrated in a few trades. Out-of-sample: 291 trades, 38.5% win rate, and the top 10 trades equal 105% of net log P&L, so the other 281 trades lose slightly. In-sample the top 10 trades were about 53% of P&L.

Separate $50 accounts at 1x would breach the drawdown limits: ETH 54% and SOL 42% out-of-sample, which would trip the desk's 40% halt. P7 is only met at the desk-blend level (1/3 weight each). In 2026 to date: BTC +16.8%, ETH -11.6%, SOL -7.2% at 1x.

Trading it live needs Binance's public 5-minute globalLongShortAccountRatio feed at every 4h close, while executing on Hyperliquid. The out-of-sample result does not depend on funding (about 0 net), so Hyperliquid's different funding does not matter much.
votes.stress:
Costs: out-of-sample Sharpe 0.96 / 0.75 / 0.54 at 1x / 2x / 3x costs, returns +78.5% / +54.3% / +33.4%. Robust.

Extra delay: +1 bar gives out-of-sample 0.80 (in-sample 1.79); +2 bars gives 1.04. Extra data lag of 65 min / 245 min / 1 day gives 0.98 / 0.80 / 0.92. No timestamp leak, and the signal decays slowly.

Out-of-sample halves: 2024-01 to 2025-04 Sharpe 0.77 (+25.2%); 2025-05 to 2026-09 Sharpe 1.16 (+42.6%). Both positive at 2x costs (0.58 / 0.93).

Per year: positive every year 2020-2025; 2026 to date -0.1%.

Other bar intervals (holding scaled to 24h): out-of-sample 2h 1.03, 8h 0.86, 12h 0.64, 1d 0.15. The effect is not specific to 4h.

Other positioning series, same rule: top-trader account ratio 0.73 out-of-sample; top-trader position ratio -0.61; taker volume ratio -0.33. Only the account-count series work.

Mechanism: the z-score correlates -0.4 to -0.55 with price's deviation from its 7-day mean, so it partly overlaps with short-term momentum. But a price-only proxy with the same z/k/H structure gives only in-sample 0.61 / out-of-sample 0.13, so the long/short ratio adds information beyond price.

Permutation null (400 random circular shifts of each coin's out-of-sample positions): null mean -0.25, standard deviation 0.64, 95th percentile 0.72. The actual 0.96 gives p = 0.0225, or about 0.066 adjusted for best of 3 finalists.

Deflated Sharpe: see issues. Out-of-sample does not clear the N=146 hurdle (1.90); clears N=3 (0.89).

Other coins: see issues. The 8-coin basket is 0.54 but depends on ADA. An 11-coin basket including BTC/ETH/SOL gives out-of-sample 0.78 with drawdown 16%.

Hyperliquid check (2025-08-21 to 2026-09-30, Binance signal applied to Hyperliquid 4h candles and hourly funding): the desk returns +14.3% with Sharpe 0.63 (drawdown 23.6%), against +14.4% / 0.63 on Binance over the same window. Hyperliquid and Binance 4h returns correlate 0.9998. By coin on Hyperliquid: ETH 0.26, SOL 0.25, and BTC tracks its Binance 1.09 (daily-return correlation 1.0). So the edge, such as it is, carries over to the venue, and recently it is almost all BTC.

Post-hoc sizing (not used for any choice): BTC 1x with ETH and SOL at 0.5x, each in its own account, gives out-of-sample per-account drawdowns of 24% / 31% / 24% and a desk Sharpe of 1.09.
votes.summary:
The claim reproduces exactly. My independent re-implementation gives in-sample Sharpe 2.08, out-of-sample 0.96, out-of-sample return +78.5%, and +54.3% at 2x costs. It passes the pre-registered P1-P8 as written. It holds up at 2x and 3x costs, an extra bar of delay, up to a day of data lag, other bar intervals, the neighbour grid and both out-of-sample halves. Hyperliquid prices and funding give the same result as Binance, and a permutation null puts the timing at p of about 0.02.

I cannot refute it, but I cannot call it REAL either:
1. The out-of-sample Sharpe does not clear the trial-count hurdle: 1.90 at the claimed 146 trials, and 2.2 at the roughly 800 cells the hunter's own log actually records.
2. On the 8 coins the hunter never used, results are mixed. Only 4 of 8 are positive. The basket's 0.54 falls to 0.23 without ADA and to 0.01 without ADA and DOGE. The short leg, which carries the BTC/ETH/SOL result, is negative on half of them.
3. All the out-of-sample profit comes from the top 10 of 291 trades.
4. ETH and SOL at 1x would breach the drawdown limits as separate accounts (54% and 42%), and in the last ~400 days only BTC has pulled its weight.

A fair reading: a real but modest effect on BTC, statistically thin, and not shown to generalise. If it is used at all, it fits best as a small, BTC-weighted sleeve on paper first, with ETH and SOL at about 0.5x.

result.family: walk-forward weak-signal model (pooled ridge, monthly expanding walk-forward, BTC/ETH/SOL, 1d)
result.summary:
I built 25 features that are known at each bar close for BTC, ETH and SOL: multi-horizon momentum, Donchian position, EMA spreads, realized vol, volume, funding level and z-score, premium, taker-buy share, OI change, retail and top-trader long/short ratios, and calendar dummies. I fitted one pooled ridge model on all three coins, refit at each month start on an expanding window with a 1-bar embargo after each label is realized. The target was the next H-day vol-normalized return. Position = the prediction divided by the std of the fitted values, mapped to an exposure, vol-targeted, 3 equal accounts. Harness costs throughout (7.5 bps/side plus real funding).

In-sample (predictions for 2021-23 only) I ran 691 variants across three rule versions:
- v1 had a flaw: the intercept dominated at high shrinkage, so those variants were simply always long.
- v2 removed the intercept and added a deadband.
- v3 dropped the calendar dummies, whose signs were unstable.

Consistent IS findings:
- Long-only beats long/short by a lot: 1d median Sharpe 1.00 vs 0.32.
- 1d bars beat 4h.
- Heavy shrinkage (alpha=10, close to weights proportional to each feature's own correlation with returns) beats OLS-like fits: median 1.10 vs 0.64.
- Short labels (H=1-3 days) are best.
- A trivial benchmark, long when the 30-day return is positive and vol-targeted, scored IS Sharpe 1.77, above every model variant (best 1.41). The model does not beat plain momentum in-sample. I did not run that benchmark out-of-sample, to keep to the 3-finalist rule.
- Pooled day-ahead rank IC is about 0, so the edge comes from being long in uptrends and flat in downtrends, not from forecasting the next day.

I took 3 finalists to out-of-sample, once each. All three meet P1-P8 as written:
- wf_full_lin: OOS Sharpe 0.75, +51%, max DD 28%.
- wf_price_bin: OOS Sharpe 0.81, +43%, max DD 20%.
- wf_full_bin: OOS Sharpe 0.80, +43%, max DD 22%.

All stay positive at 2x costs, and every P6 neighbour is positive (median OOS Sharpe 0.66-0.73). None beats the desk on its own (desk OOS 0.85). They are additive: correlation with the desk is 0.34-0.43 over the full period (0.50-0.63 OOS), and a 50/50 blend lifts OOS Sharpe from 0.85 to 0.91-0.92.

Caveats:
- The three finalists are one finding, not three (0.77-0.93 correlated with each other).
- The finding is in effect a long-only, multi-horizon trend-following book, a second trend book next to the desk.
- The flow and positioning features did not improve OOS results (full 0.80 vs price-only 0.81).
- 2025 was flat for the model (+0.2% / +4.5%) while the desk made +23.6%.
- The data are survivorship-biased (SOL's 2021 run inflates the in-sample numbers), and 691 IS trials were run.

If the desk adds one, wf_price_bin is the simplest: price-only features, max 1.5x account leverage, OOS max DD 20%, +10% in 2026 YTD vs desk +4.4%.

candidates.name: wf_full_lin
candidates.coins: BTC,ETH,SOL (3 equal accounts)
candidates.params: fset=full_nocal (14 price + 11 flow features, no calendar), H=1d label, alpha=10, smoothing S=7d EWM, map=lin clip(z/2,-1,1), long-only, deadband 0.05, tv=1.0 per account, cap 5x (max used 2.5x)
candidates.rules: Data: H.klines(coin,'1d') BTC/ETH/SOL, H.funding, H.premium, H.metrics. Features at close of day t (wf.build): sigma=EWM(span30) std of daily log returns; mom_h=log(C_t/C_{t-h})/(sigma*sqrt(h)), h=1,3,7,14,30,60,120; donch_N=(C-mid)/(max-min) over highs/lows of last N=20,60 days incl t; ema(10,40),(25,100) spread/(C*sigma); log(std7/std60); 365d z of log std30; log(vol7/vol60); fund3=mean funding print over (close-3d,close] and its 90d z; prem1=mean hourly premium close of the last 24h and its 90d z; taker_buy/volume over 1d and 7d as 90d z; OI log change 1d,7d /sigma (metrics asof close); 90d z of 1d-mean count_long_short_ratio, sum_toptrader_long_short_ratio, log sum_taker_long_short_vol_ratio. Label y_t=log(C_{t+1}/C_t)/sigma_t clipped +/-5. At each month start M from 2021-01: training rows (all 3 coins pooled) with open(t)+3 days <= M; standardise columns with training mean/std, clip +/-4, NaN->0; ridge beta=(Z'Z+10*n*I)^-1 Z'(y-mean y), no intercept in prediction; s=std(Z beta) on training rows; z_t=(Z_t beta)/s for each day of month M. a=clip(z/2,-1,1), set a<0 to 0, EWM span 7 (adjust=False), |a|<0.05 -> 0. Account exposure w=a*1.0/(sigma*sqrt(365)), cap 5. Portfolio weight w/3 per coin, H.backtest_portfolio(…,'1d') (decide at daily close, fill next open, 7.5 bps/side on |delta|, real funding). No stops; exits only via signal.

candidates.notes: A controlled test of H2 (does adding the flow features help?): against wf_price_bin, adding them did NOT help OOS (Sharpe 0.80 vs 0.81, 32% more entries, return at 2x costs 0.34 vs 0.36). 0.93 correlated with wf_price_bin, so it is not an independent result. Per-year returns: 2024 +33%, 2025 +1.2%, 2026 YTD +5.9%.

negative_results: v1 design (unpenalised training-mean intercept divided by the std of the shrunk fitted values): at alpha=10 it degenerated to always long (identical +98.5% in 2021 across configs). Fixed in v2 by removing the intercept. 144 trials.

Long/short versions: 1d median IS Sharpe (2021-23) 0.32 full / 0.24 price vs long-only 1.00 / 0.75; 4h LS 0.16 / 0.02. Model-predicted shorts lose money, consistent with the desk's rejected BTC/SOL shorts.
4h bars: worse than 1d for every setting (LO full median 0.79 vs 1.00; best 1.02 vs 1.24).
Low shrinkage (alpha=0.1, close to OLS): 1d LO median IS Sharpe 0.64 vs 1.10 at alpha=10. Freely fitted multivariate weights overfit; near-univariate weights are better.
Longer label horizons: 1d LO median IS Sharpe H=1: 0.97, H=3: 1.02, H=7: 0.88, H=14: 0.81.
Calendar dummies (day-of-week, hour): unstable coefficient signs (dow3 sign stability 6%, dow6 31%); dropping them raised the best IS Sharpe from 1.24 to 1.34.

Trivial benchmark, long when 30-day return > 0, vol-targeted: IS (2021-23) Sharpe 1.77 (long/short 1.68) vs best model 1.41. The model did not beat plain momentum in-sample. The benchmark was not taken OOS, to stay within 3 finalists.

Prediction skill: pooled day-ahead rank IC of the model z-score is between -0.013 and +0.017 for all variants (H-day label IC at most 0.06). There is no real day-ahead forecasting skill; the profit comes from being long in uptrends and flat in downtrends.

H2 (flow features add value): IS medians favoured the full set (1.00-1.04 vs 0.78-0.86), but OOS the full set was no better (0.80 vs 0.81) and traded more. Funding level/z and premium carried small, sign-unstable weights (fund3 sign stability 64%, fundz 17% in IS fits).
Smoothing with EWM before the deadband was added made long-only positions never return to 0 (5 entries in 3 years). The deadband of 0.05 was required for meaningful entry counts.
observations: The most stable non-price signal is contrarian. The z-score of Binance's retail account long/short ratio (count_long_short_ratio, 1d mean vs 90d) carries the largest model weight, negative (-0.18 in IS fits, -0.21 in OOS fits), with 100% sign stability over 69 monthly refits: when retail is crowded long, forward returns are lower. Top-trader ratio z is also negative. Even so, adding these features did not improve OOS trading results.
OI change turned from about 0 in IS fits to clearly negative in OOS fits (oi1 -0.04 to -0.11, oi7 +0.01 to -0.10): rising open interest predicted weaker next-day returns in 2024-26.

All momentum horizons (3d through 120d), Donchian position and EMA spreads carry positive weights with 91-100% sign stability. The model is in effect a long-only multi-horizon trend follower and largely re-discovers what the desk already trades.

The desk's main gap is time out of the market. A daily long-only trend book that holds about 40-60% of the time is 0.34-0.43 correlated with the desk over the full period (0.50-0.63 OOS) and raises the desk's OOS Sharpe from 0.85 to about 0.92 in a 50/50 blend.

2025 was the model's weak year (flat) while the desk made +23.6%; 2024 was the reverse (model +24% to +54%, desk +13%). The two trend books make money in different trend phases, which is where the diversification comes from.
2026 YTD: equal-weight desk +4.4% (BTC account -11%); wf_price_bin +10.2%; wf_full_lin -2.0%.

SOL decays out-of-sample for this family as it does for the desk: per-coin SOL Sharpe 1.6-1.9 in 2021-23 vs 0.2-0.6 OOS. The universe was chosen in hindsight, and SOL's 2021 run flatters every in-sample number.
Funding is a material cost for any long-biased book: about 10% of equity paid over the 2.75 OOS years at an average exposure of about 0.3x for wf_full_lin, versus about 4% in fees and slippage.

Multiple testing: 691 in-sample variants (heavily correlated) plus 39 OOS neighbour runs that were used only for P6. The three finalists are 0.77-0.93 correlated with each other, so count them as one finding.

Suggested follow-up for whoever covers trend portfolios: compare a plain vol-targeted sign(30d momentum) long-only book against the desk out-of-sample. In-sample it beat this model (1.77 vs 1.41) and is simpler to run.

votes.summary:
The claim reproduces. My independent rebuild gets OOS Sharpe 0.91 and in-sample 1.20 against the hunter's 0.80 and 1.07, with nearly identical positions (0.97 daily-return correlation), and the hunter's own script reproduces its numbers exactly. On BTC/ETH/SOL it passes P1-P8 as written, and my own neighbour grid also passes P6.

It does not hold up beyond that. On four groups of other 2020-listed coins it is positive in only 2 of 4 and beats plain vol-targeted always-long in only 1 of 4. Its OOS Sharpe has a t-stat of about 1.15 and is far below what 691 trials would produce by chance (about 2.18; 0.89 even counting only the 3 finalists). Its excess over passive long or a simple 30-day momentum rule is not significant (t about 1.2-1.3).

What it mostly is: a vol-targeted, long-only, multi-horizon momentum book that sits out bear markets. Recent results are about zero: on Hyperliquid over the last ~418 days the hunter's version made -2.2% (Sharpe -0.01), Hyperliquid funding cost about twice Binance's, and the full model loses money there at 2x costs. The flow features add nothing; the price-only twin is equal or better.

It is not refuted, because it reproduces and some generalisation exists. But it falls short of REAL: the edge is weak, concentrated in the selected coins, and fading. My code and notes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c67283e4-8e62-5bce-a0e4-e537e0ac564b/scratchpad/edge/verify/walkforward_model_wf_full_bin_independent_p/ (PLAN.md, vwf.py; t1.py prints the main numbers, t2-t8 the other tests, hl/ holds the Hyperliquid data).

result.family: desk_upgrades_p: improvements to the desk's own 2h Donchian-60 / EMA100>EMA400 breakout, run on the real engine (subclassed, reproduces desk.backtest.run bit-for-bit)
result.summary: I tested 44 pre-registered variants of the live desk on the real engine (108 runs, 2020-23 in-sample only). The engine was extended by subclassing Desk and SimBroker in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c67283e4-8e62-5bce-a0e4-e537e0ac564b/scratchpad/edge/hunters/desk_upgrades_p/xdesk.py; with no extensions it reproduces desk.backtest.run exactly for BTC, ETH and SOL. My baseline in-sample desk Sharpe was 1.51 (BTC 1.41, ETH 0.71, SOL 0.76), matching the brief. Selection rule: beat 1.51 by at least 0.10 and improve at least 2 of 3 coins. None of the following passed it: re-entry after a stop-out (best 1.37), time stops (best 1.53), trailing on highs (best 1.36), trail width by volatility regime (best 1.51), pyramiding (best 1.39), slow-ATR sizing (best 1.49), lookback ensembles (best 1.54) and a daily SMA trend filter (best 1.53). Only the per-coin stop/trail width test qualified: in-sample it picked ETH 3.5 ATR (0.96 vs 0.71) and SOL 4.0 ATR (1.30 vs 0.76). That became the single finalist F1, run out-of-sample once. Desk with BTC unchanged, ETH 3.5, SOL 4.0: Sharpe in-sample 1.65 / out-of-sample 0.92, against the baseline's 1.51 / 0.85. Out-of-sample return +49.2% vs +46.2%; at 2x costs +37.7%; max drawdown 12.3%. All 8 neighbours were positive, median Sharpe 0.93. Correlation with the desk is 0.976, but a 50/50 blend scores 0.889 vs 0.852. So F1 PASSES P1-P8 as written. The honest reading is narrower. The gain is small (+0.07 desk Sharpe; a paired block bootstrap gives a 5-95% range of -0.09 to +0.25, with a 23% chance it is zero or negative). It comes almost entirely from ETH: out-of-sample 0.71 vs 0.52, and the ETH leg passes on its own. The SOL leg did not hold: SOL out-of-sample 0.19 vs 0.24, failing P2 and the per-coin P8. The idea also first surfaced post hoc in earlier desk work. Why BTC is losing in 2026 (descriptive only): breakouts without follow-through in a range-bound year. 13 trades, 23% winners, average -0.16R, best trade only +2.15R, median MFE (largest open profit before exit) 1.57 ATR vs 3.01 in-sample. Entries were not later than usual and stops were not too tight. None of the variants chosen on 2020-23 would have rescued 2026.

Initial stop = entry close -/+ k*ATR(28); chandelier trail = best close since entry -/+ k*ATR(28), only ratchets; exit on EMA flip. k = 3.0 BTC, 3.5 ETH, 4.0 SOL. Size = equity*risk/(k*ATR), capped at 5x equity, so a wider stop means a smaller position. H-s for BTC (information only): k=2.5 1.30, 3.5 1.23, 4.0 1.19, 4.5 1.33 vs 3.0 1.41 in-sample. BTC's 3 ATR stop is the in-sample best; keep it.

Descriptive only, not a test: 2026 BTC under the in-sample-best variant of each hypothesis: re-entry R30 -22.6%, trail-on-highs k4 -16.2%, ensemble 40/60/180 -16.5%, pyramiding -10.6%, vol-regime trail -10.4%, slow-ATR sizing -7.7%, daily SMA50 and time stop N48 -11.4% (same as baseline). None would have rescued 2026.
observations: The engine can be extended without editing the repo. /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c67283e4-8e62-5bce-a0e4-e537e0ac564b/scratchpad/edge/hunters/desk_upgrades_p/xdesk.py subclasses Desk and SimBroker; with no extensions it gives curves and trades identical to desk.backtest.run (check_equiv.py). One full 2020-26 run takes about 1.2 s, not 10-30 s.
The EMA-flip exit almost never fires: 0 of 118 BTC trades, 1 of 236 ETH, 0 of 107 SOL. The chandelier stop always exits first, so EMA100/400 only matters as an entry filter.

ETH and SOL prefer wider trails than BTC in-sample, under three separate parameterisations: plain stop/trail width k, the vol-regime trail with alpha=1, and trailing on highs at k>=3.5. Out-of-sample this held for ETH (3.5 ATR: 0.71 vs 0.52; 4.0: 0.75) but not for SOL (4.0: 0.19 vs 0.24).
SOL's out-of-sample Sharpe is weak at every stop width tested (0.19-0.32). The baseline SOL account (0.24) would itself fail P2.

Why BTC is losing in 2026: 13 trades, 23% winners (44% in-sample), average -0.16R (+0.84R in-sample), best trade +2.15R (+14.5R in-sample), median MFE 1.57 ATR (3.01 in-sample). Losses cluster in 5 failed breakouts from 11-22 April plus 2 in early May. Entries were not later than usual (median 4.9 ATR above EMA100 vs 4.2 in-sample; breakout margin 0.65 ATR, same as in-sample). Volatility was lower (ATR 0.88% vs 1.16%). The uptrend filter was on for only 47% of bars, and buy-and-hold was -5%. The losers' MFE was 0.5-2.4 ATR, and wider BTC stops were worse in-sample, so stops being too tight is not the cause. It is a range year with no fat-tail winner, the normal failure mode of a breakout strategy.

BTC's -11% over 9 months is at the edge of in-sample experience: the worst rolling 273-day in-sample return was -13.3%, and only 0.3% of windows fell below -11%. The 2026 BTC drawdown (27.9%) is deeper than any in-sample drawdown (22.5%) and is the closest the 5%-risk account has come to the 40% halt.

Realised leverage at live settings: BTC median 1.70x (max 3.96x), ETH 0.47x (max 1.85x), SOL 0.36x (max 1.0x). At 2% risk the ETH and SOL accounts carry small exposure, which is why they add little return to the desk.
Wider ETH stops are also more cost-robust: at 2x costs ETH OOS is +33.9% at 3.5 ATR vs +20.2% at 3.0, because it trades less (94 vs 105 OOS entries).
Survivorship bias does not apply to this family: the coins are the desk's fixed three, though SOL Binance data only starts in 2020-09.

votes.reproduced: The hunter's final_stopwidth.py re-runs in 18 seconds and produces JSON byte-identical to their saved final_stopwidth.json. Desk in-sample Sharpe 1.651 (return +256%, max DD 9.7%, 214 entries). Out-of-sample: Sharpe 0.920, return +49.2%, max DD 12.3%, 193 entries. OOS at 2x costs: +37.7%. Neighbour median OOS Sharpe 0.933, 8/8 neighbours positive. Correlation with the desk 0.976; 50/50 blend 0.889 vs desk 0.852. Baseline recomputed: 1.515 / 0.852. Per coin: ETH k3.5 0.961 / 0.708 vs k3.0 0.708 / 0.521; SOL k4.0 1.304 / 0.192 vs 0.762 / 0.242. I re-ran everything independently (vlib.py: the unmodified repo Desk and SimBroker loop) and got the same numbers. P1-P8 do pass as written.
issues: No look-ahead found in the engine. Donchian uses only prior bars; EMA and Wilder ATR use bars up to t. Decisions are made at close t and fill at open t+1. The trailing stop set at close t is first checked against bar t+1's high/low, and gaps fill at the open. Funding is the sum of prints in (open, close] and is charged while held. Fees and slippage are charged on every open and close, for both ETH shorts and longs. short_stop_atr is None, so k really applies to ETH shorts too.

Data is clean. The repo's native Binance 2h bars match the harness's 1h-to-2h resample on all but 1 of 29,580 ETH bars (a 2024-10-28 open). There are no bad OHLC rows; SOL has 2 gaps (largest 37 bars). Funding covers the full period.

The SOL leg's in-sample gain is mostly an artifact of the $50 account. A $10 minimum-ticket gate meets risk = equity x 2% / (k x ATR): wider stops mean smaller tickets, so more high-volatility SOL entries get skipped. In-sample SOL bars blocked only by the ticket gate: 20 at k3.0, 64 at k4.0, 102 at k4.5. Entries drop from 51 to 33 at k4.0. With the gate off, SOL's baseline in-sample Sharpe is 0.27, not 0.76. The SOL k4.0 in-sample gain also sits almost entirely in 2023 (+51.7% vs +12.3%; in 2021 it was worse: +6.6% vs +19.1%). Out of sample it doesn't improve SOL at all (0.19 vs 0.24).

The hypothesis was contaminated before the test. The brief says the wider-stop idea for ETH/SOL had already been seen on full-period data, including OOS. The hunter's PLAN then gave H-s special treatment: it was the only hypothesis selected per coin with a per-coin +0.10 gate. Under the uniform rule used for the other 8 hypotheses (one shared setting, desk in-sample Sharpe at least 1.61), H-s's best shared setting (s_k4.5, 1.52) would have failed and never reached OOS. c2_reg1.0 would also have qualified per coin (ETH 1.00, SOL 1.03) but wasn't given that route.

The in-sample selection is consistent with noise. Across the 44 trials, in-sample desk Sharpe has a cross-trial sd of 0.112, so the expected best-of-noise uplift is +0.25. F1's 1.651 sits below the baseline-plus-uplift bar of 1.76; the deflated probability that it truly clears that bar is 0.36-0.38. The paired daily-difference t-stat in-sample is 1.53 for the desk and 0.88 for ETH.

The OOS improvement is not statistically different from zero. The paired daily-difference t-stat is 0.34 for the desk and 0.69 for ETH. The probability that F1's OOS Sharpe beats the baseline's 0.852 is 0.55. The hunter's own bootstrap agrees: P(gain <= 0) = 0.23 for the desk.

The gain rests on a handful of days and trades. Removing the 5 OOS days where F1 beats the baseline most flips the desk result (0.742 vs 0.778), and does the same for ETH (0.456 vs 0.528). The ETH OOS gain of about $15.8 comes mostly from one trade: k3.5 held the July 2025 rally for +$18.0, where k3.0 was stopped and re-entered for about +$9.6. I couldn't find a code flaw. The engine has no look-ahead, costs and funding are charged on every leg including ETH shorts, the data is consistent, and the hunter's numbers reproduce exactly. F1 also survives 2x and 3x costs and one extra bar of delay, and its gain over the baseline even grows with costs because it trades less.

I wrote my own bar-by-bar engine from the rules text (sim.py), using harness data and the harness cost and timing rules. I did not use the hunter's code or the repo engine. To check the engine, I first ran it at k=3 against baseline_daily.csv. Daily Sharpe IS/OOS came out as BTC 1.45/0.85 (file: 1.41/0.87), ETH 0.72/0.53 (0.71/0.52), SOL 0.81/0.24 (0.76/0.24) and desk 1.55/0.84 (1.51/0.85). Total returns matched within 0.5% and daily correlation was 0.92-0.94.

The in-sample k grid {2.5..4.5} gave the same per-coin argmax as the claim: BTC 3.0, ETH 3.5, SOL 4.0.

F1 desk, mine vs claim:
- IS Sharpe 1.684 vs 1.651; IS return +252.9% vs +256.5%; IS max DD 9.5% vs 9.7%.
- OOS Sharpe 0.904 vs 0.920; OOS return +49.4% vs +49.2%; OOS max DD 12.4% vs 12.3%.
- Entries IS 214 / OOS 193, identical to the claim.
- OOS at 2x cost +37.4% vs +37.7%.
- Neighbour median OOS Sharpe 0.915 vs 0.933, with 9/9 cells positive.
- 50/50 blend OOS Sharpe 0.891 vs desk 0.852 (claim 0.889 vs 0.852).
- Correlation with the desk 0.90 full / 0.94 OOS (claim 0.976). The gap is because the hunter ran the exact repo engine that produced baseline_daily and I used my own.

Per coin, IS/OOS Sharpe: ETH k3.5 0.98/0.72 vs k3 0.72/0.53; SOL k4 1.35/0.19 vs k3 0.81/0.24.

Pass rule P1-P8 at the desk level: it passes as written. The claim reproduces.
issues: The gain is small and statistically indistinguishable from zero. Desk OOS Sharpe gain is +0.066 (paired stationary-block bootstrap 5-95% -0.09..+0.26, P(gain<=0)=0.26). Even the in-sample gain the selection was made on is not significant (+0.13, P(<=0)=0.13). ETH: +0.19 (P(<=0)=0.16). SOL: -0.05 (P(<=0)=0.56).

Deflated Sharpe: with N=44 trials, noise alone gives an expected best Sharpe of about 1.66 over T=2.75 OOS years and 1.38 over 4 IS years. The OOS Sharpe of 0.90 does not clear 1.66 (single-test t is about 1.5), though the existing desk doesn't clear it either. The relevant number is the upgrade itself. Between variants this highly correlated (rho about 0.94), the noise-best Sharpe gain at N=44 is about 0.58; the claimed +0.07 is nowhere near it.

About 40% of the desk-level gain is a sizing side effect, not the stop. A wider stop means a smaller ETH/SOL position, which shifts desk risk toward BTC, the highest-Sharpe leg. Control: k=3 with ETH/SOL risk scaled down to give the same entry size as F1 gets desk OOS Sharpe 0.863, against 0.838 for the baseline and 0.904 for F1.

The SOL leg fails on its own out-of-sample (0.19 vs 0.24 at k=3). Its in-sample argmax is driven by one year: 2023 returns +51.7% at k=4 vs +12.3% at k=3, while 2021 is worse (+6.6% vs +19.1%). SOL's in-sample Sharpe also depends heavily on the $10 minimum ticket on a $50 account: at k=3 it is 0.81 with the ticket rule and 0.28 without it.

The specific ETH value (3.5) does not generalize. On 22 other universe coins, k=3.5 vs 3.0 OOS has a mean Sharpe change of -0.034 and improves only 32% of coins. Generality favours much wider stops: k=4.0 gives +0.12 mean (59% of coins improve) and k=4.5 gives +0.32 (77%). The in-sample argmax hits the grid edge (4.5) on 12 of the 17 coins listed early. Most of these coins have negative Sharpe at every k, so this is mostly losing less, not a tradeable edge. The universe is survivorship-biased.

The in-sample and out-of-sample Sharpe surfaces disagree, which points to noise. BTC in-sample is non-monotonic in k (1.30/1.45/1.25/1.22/1.36). A single k shared by all coins would have picked 3.0 in-sample (1.55) yet scores best out-of-sample at 3.5 (0.99). BTC's own best OOS k is 3.5 (0.97 vs 0.85), the opposite of its in-sample choice.

ETH's OOS gain sits entirely in 2025-05..2026-09 (Sharpe 1.44 vs 1.11). In 2024-01..2025-04 both widths lose about the same (-0.67 vs -0.68). By year, ETH k3.5 is better in 4 of 7 years and slightly worse in 3, including 2024 (-8.9% vs -6.9%).

Post-hoc contamination, as the hunter admits: the 4-ATR idea for ETH/SOL was first noticed on full-period data. The hunter's per-coin selection gate for this hypothesis also gave it more freedom than the others had (2 coins x 5 grid values vs one shared setting).

P8 is weak here. A modification of the desk itself, with correlation about 0.94-0.98, passes the 50/50 blend test whenever its Sharpe is even slightly above the desk's. Passing it says nothing about being additive.

Hyperliquid funding was about 2x Binance's over the overlap (BTC/ETH about 0.0015% per 2h bar vs 0.0006-0.0008%). This is small at these exposures but goes against the Binance-based numbers. My HL funding bucketing ignores the roughly 18 ms print offset, which is immaterial.

votes.summary:
The claim reproduces closely with an independent engine and passes P1-P8 at the desk level as written. Entry counts match exactly and desk OOS Sharpe is 0.90 vs the claimed 0.92. Direction holds at 2x/3x costs, with an extra bar of delay, in both OOS halves and on Hyperliquid's own data.

It is not a real edge, though:
- The gain (+0.07 desk Sharpe) is statistically zero (bootstrap P(gain<=0)=0.26) and far below the noise threshold for 44 trials.
- About 40% of it is a sizing side effect: smaller ETH/SOL legs shift desk risk toward BTC.
- SOL's k=4 fails on its own OOS and its in-sample pick rests on one year (2023).
- ETH's specific 3.5 does not transfer to other coins: only 32% of 22 improve.
- What does transfer is a broader tendency for much wider stops (4.0-4.5) to cut losses on alts where this breakout loses money anyway.

So the verdict is UNCERTAIN, not REFUTED. Moving ETH to 3.5 ATR is a harmless paper tweak with weak support (positive in OOS, at 2x costs and on HL), and should be labelled as an experiment, not a validated edge. SOL should stay at 3.0, and the desk should not expect a measurable improvement.

result.summary:
Execution-realism audit of the current desk. All scripts and data are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c67283e4-8e62-5bce-a0e4-e537e0ac564b/scratchpad/edge/audit_p/exec/. PLAN.md logs 55 variants; 2 maker finalists went out-of-sample once each. My full-history replay matches baseline_daily.csv (correlation 1.0; Sharpe 1.41/0.88, 0.71/0.52, 0.76/0.24).

Main finding: the paper ledger does NOT fill at the live price when the job runs. Both paper.step and the sim fill orders at the Hyperliquid (HL) bar open and stops at min(open, stop), exactly like the backtest. So GitHub's scheduling lag costs paper nothing. Paper differs from the backtest only through venue data, while live adds execution and code risk.

Measured gaps:
(a) Venue: HL prices sit 1.6-1.9 bps above Binance (sd about 3 bps), and 2h returns correlate at 0.9996. Breakout and trend signals disagree on 0-4 of 3,657 bars per coin. HL funding ran 2-4 pp a year higher. Replaying the desk on HL vs Binance data over 2025-08 to 2026-09 gave BTC -2.75% vs -3.47%, ETH +13.19% vs +13.16%, SOL +3.40% vs +10.03%. The SOL gap comes from one HL wick that stopped out the year's best winner early: path noise, not bias.
(b) Latency: there is no consistent drift after the close. Pooled over 461 entries it is +2.3 bps at 5 min (t=1.4) and -0.1 bps at 10 min, and the sign flips between in-sample and out-of-sample. Latency adds noise (sd 35-48 bps per trade), not a mean cost.
(c) Stops: checked at 5m resolution, the stop fills match the 2h sim on all 460 stop exits (0 bps difference, no gapped opens). A bot that only checked stops when the job runs would on average have done as well or better, but with a 10th percentile of -100 to -195 bps, so keep the resting exchange stops.
(d) Maker entries: post-only entries with a taker chase if not filled PASS P1-P8 as an overlay on the same strategy. Desk out-of-sample Sharpe goes from 0.854 to 0.897 (60-min window) or 0.901 (15-min window); it holds at 2x costs; all 8 neighbours land at 0.88-0.91; P8 passes only via the blend clause (correlation 0.9997). It is not a new edge, and about half the modelled saving is the 3 bps slippage that the live HL book (spread 0.12-0.93 bps) says is not really paid at this ticket size.
(e) Tiny accounts: the $10 minimum blocked 18 SOL signals, 1 ETH and 0 BTC, already inside the backtest. Rounding to HL size steps cuts SOL size by 2.4% on average; the effect is 0.08 pp a year or less.

Fixes ranked by dollar impact on 3 x $50:
1. LiveBroker hardcodes BTC/USDC: an ETH or SOL live desk would trade BTC at about 33x (whole account at risk; live only).
2. A failed stop placement leaves the position unprotected, and nothing re-places the stop (tail risk up to the account).
3. Maker entries: about +$0.86 a year on the honest 3 bps fee saving; +$1.6 a year in the backtest's cost model.
4. Lower the modelled entry slippage from 3 bps to about 0.5 bps for $50-250 tickets: paper understates live by about $0.78 a year (calibration only).
5. HL funding: about -$0.29 a year, mostly BTC.
6. Everything else is under $0.1 a year or noise.

In dollars all the cost items are small, because the accounts are $50. The large dollar items are the two live-broker bugs. On your question about more than 2 agents: this is one auditor's report, and nothing here depends on how many agents run the audit.

findings.title: LiveBroker ignores the coin: an ETH or SOL live desk sends its orders to BTC-PERP
findings.evidence: /home/user/btc-perp-desk/desk/brokers/live.py:29-35 SYMBOLS={'hyperliquid':'BTC/USDC:USDC',...}; live.py:65 self.symbol = SYMBOLS[self.venue] (p.market.symbol is never used); desk/__main__.py:292-293,324 common() adds --coin choices BTC/ETH/SOL to the 'live' parser, so `python -m desk live --coin ETH` is accepted. Repro with a stub exchange (no network): an ETH desk with max_notional 50 sends ('BTC/USDC:USDC','buy',0.02) = about $1,652 of BTC at 82.6k on a $50 account (about 33x); a SOL desk sends 0.3 BTC = about $24.8k.
findings.impact: Live only (paper is not affected). The first ETH or SOL live entry would open a BTC position 30-500x larger than intended. The whole $50 account, or more on cross margin, is at risk on the first trade.
findings.fix: Build the ccxt symbol from p.market.symbol (f'{coin}/USDC:USDC' for hyperliquid), and assert on startup that the exchange market matches the feed coin. Add a test that LiveBroker(params_for('ETH')).symbol starts with 'ETH/'.

findings.title: A failed stop placement after a live entry leaves the position with no exchange stop, and nothing re-places it
findings.evidence: live.py:140-158 _open fills the market order, sets Position(stop=o.stop), then calls _place_stop; if that raises, stop_order_id stays None but position.stop is non-zero. runner.py:84-88 re-protects only if `not broker.position.stop`. live.py:217-219 check_stop_price only syncs and never enforces a local stop. A new stop is placed only when the trail ratchets up (update_stop), which never happens if price falls. Repro: the stub exchange rejects the stop; the output shows position open=True, local stop=80000, exchange stop id=None, runner re-place condition False.
findings.impact: Tail risk. At up to 5x leverage, a 20% adverse move with no stop wipes out the account. The probability is unknown; it depends on HL rejects or 429s at the moment of entry.
findings.fix: Make the runner track stop_order_id, not position.stop: if a position exists with no confirmed exchange stop, retry placement every poll and flatten after N failures. Alternatively, send entry and stop together as one order group (HL supports TP/SL attached to the entry).

findings.title: Post-only (maker) entries with a taker chase cut costs and pass P1-P8 as an execution overlay (modest, and half of it is modelled slippage)
findings.evidence: In-sample grid (24 variants, maker_grid_is.csv): bid at the fill-bar open, filled only if a Binance 5m low trades strictly below it (assumes we are last in the queue). Skipping unfilled entries loses money because the unfilled ones are the runaway winners (BTC unfilled trades average +878 bps of equity vs +352 filled), so the fallback is a taker chase. Finalists chosen on in-sample data: k=0 with 60-min and 15-min windows. Fill rates: BTC 114/118, ETH 232/236, SOL 107/107 at 60 min. Equal-weight desk, native sizing: baseline in-sample/out-of-sample Sharpe 1.515/0.854 and OOS return +46.3%; 60-min version 1.546/0.897 and +49.3%; 15-min version 1.542/0.901 and +49.7%. At 2x costs OOS return is +40.9%/+41.3% vs +33.7% baseline. Neighbours' OOS Sharpe 0.883-0.907, all 8 positive. Max drawdown 14.2%, leverage ≤5x (BTC 5% risk, ETH/SOL 2%). Correlation with the desk 0.9997, so P8 passes only via the blend (0.875 vs 0.854).
findings.impact: Modelled: +2.9 to +3.4 pp desk return over 2.75 years out-of-sample (about +1.1 pp a year, +0.8 pp CAGR over the full period), about $1.6 a year on 3 x $50. Honest version (only the 3 bps fee saving, 4.5→1.5 bps, because the 3 bps taker slippage is mostly not paid at this size): about 3 bps per entry, worth BTC 1.0%/yr ($0.49), ETH 0.53%/yr ($0.27), SOL 0.21%/yr ($0.10), about $0.86 a year in total.

findings.fix: Live entries: post an HL ALO (post-only) bid at the best bid as soon as the bar closes, leave it 15-60 min, then cancel and send a taker order. Keep stop exits as taker stop-market (460 of 461 exits are stop or trail exits, so there is no maker opportunity on exits). Caveats: the fill model uses Binance 5m lows as a proxy for HL; and since the paper sim fills at the bar open, paper would need a maker-fill model to show this saving.

findings.title: The sim's 3 bps taker slippage is about 6-25x the real HL half-spread for $10-$800 tickets: paper and backtest understate live market orders
findings.evidence: hl_book.json (3 snapshots, 2026-10-12 22:01 UTC): spreads BTC 0.12, ETH 0.40, SOL 0.93 bps; top-of-book size $10k-$410k; depth within 10 bps $2.9M-$11.5M. findings.fix: Split Costs.slippage_bps into an entry value (about 1 bps at this size) and a stop value (3 bps), and log the real fill vs mid on the first live fills to calibrate. Do not use the lower number to justify more leverage.

findings.title: Hyperliquid funding ran 2-4 pp a year above Binance in the overlap; the backtest uses Binance funding

findings.title: Paper fills at the HL bar open, not at the live price when the job runs, so GitHub scheduling lag costs paper nothing; post-close drift is not significant
findings.evidence: desk/paper.py:116-121: broker.fill_pending(forming.open, ...) for the forming bar; closed bars catch up with fill_pending(bar.open) at paper.py:91. The premise in the brief (paper fills at the live price when it runs) does not match the code. GitHub API (b_latency.json): only 13 of about 283 expected scheduled runs were delivered over 70.8 h (4.6%); 36 workflow_dispatch runs at about :07. Delay from each even-hour close to the first run: median 7.8 min, p90 49 min, max 299 min; 29 of 35 closes picked up within 15 min. Entry drift on Binance 5m vs the bar open, pooled over 461 entries: +2.3 bps at 5 min (t=1.38), -0.1 bps at 10 min (t=-0.05). By coin: BTC 5-min drift is +5.7 in-sample vs +0.7 out-of-sample; ETH +6.4 vs -5.4 (sign flips); sd 27-57 bps.
findings.impact: Paper: 0 bps by construction. Live runner (15 s poll, executes about 5-20 s after the close): about 0. If live ever ran on the GitHub cadence: expected cost about 0 ± noise. At the 5-min point estimate it would be BTC 1.1%/yr, ETH 0.2%/yr, SOL 0.24%/yr, but none of these is statistically different from 0. Latency adds about 35-48 bps of per-trade noise.

findings.title: Stops between runs: paper fills at the stop level (resting-stop semantics); a 5m check gives the same fills; polling-only stops would add a fat left tail
findings.evidence: sim.py:105-117 check_stop_bar fills at min(open, stop) on the bar low, whenever the run happens; paper also checks the forming bar so far (paper.py:118-121). Over 460 stop exits, the 5m-resolution fill (first 5m bar crossing the stop, min(open_5m, stop)) differs from the 2h sim by 0.0 bps (p5 0.0), with 0 gapped opens. If a stop were only checked at runs (even hour + 7 min), detection lag would average 52-69 min after the crossing, and the exit price minus the stop would be: mean BTC -11.6/+0.1, ETH +2.7/+20.0, SOL +91.9/+24.3 bps (in-sample/out-of-sample), p10 -100 to -195 bps. Price 30 min after a stop is above it on average (+7 to +58 bps), meaning post-stop reversion.

A polling-only implementation would have similar mean P&L but 1-2% worst-decile losses per stop. Speculative: HL stop triggers fire on mark price, not last trade, so some trade-price wicks that stop paper out would not trigger live (could favour live).

findings.title: Tiny-account effects: the $10 minimum blocks SOL signals (and happened to help); rounding to HL size steps cuts SOL size 2.4% and rejects 2 ETH entries live
findings.evidence: e_tiny.json, full-history replay: signals blocked by the ticket_usd gate: BTC 0, ETH 1, SOL 18 episodes (median would-be notional SOL $6.77). Removing the minimum changes CAGR by ETH -0.34 pp and SOL -3.19 pp (12 extra SOL trades lost money), so the gate acted as an accidental high-volatility filter; it is already in the backtest. HL size steps (meta: BTC 5, ETH 4, SOL 2 decimals) truncate size by an average 0.06% / 0.34% / 2.41%; 2 ETH entries fall below $10 after truncation (live rejects them, paper does not). CAGR effect -0.02 / +0.23 / -0.08 pp full period, about 0 out-of-sample. Smallest notionals: ETH $10.04, SOL $10.15, BTC $60.7.
findings.impact: Under $0.05 a year. SOL and ETH tickets ($22 and $38 on average) sit near the $10 minimum, so after a 30-50% drawdown most ETH/SOL signals would be blocked.
findings.fix: Mirror HL's size step and the post-rounding $10 check in SimBroker so paper skips what live skips. Do not remove the min-notional gate on the strength of this result (it was found post hoc).

findings.title: When the exchange stop fills, live sync books the exit at the current mid, not the actual fill
findings.evidence: live.py:103-115 sync(): px = price or pos.stop, where price is the mid passed by check_stop_price(mid) at the next poll. The trade's gross P&L and fee are computed at that px. Engine._update_risk counts consecutive losses from t.net_pnl (engine.py:131-140). Cash is re-read from the exchange, so equity itself stays correct.
findings.impact: With a 15 s poll the error is a few bps per stop. If the runner was down while the stop filled, the booked price is off by the post-stop move (5m study: mean 0 to +90 bps, p10 -100 to -195 bps). That can flip a recorded win or loss and mis-count the 5-loss cooldown. $ effect about 0; it is a ledger-integrity issue.
findings.fix: Fetch the stop order's fill (fetch_order(stop_order_id) or fetch_my_trades) and book that price and fee.

findings.title: The paper-only spread/depth gates never bind on HL today; the BTC depth figure covers only about 2.5 bps

results.title: LiveBroker ignores the coin: an ETH or SOL live desk sends its orders to BTC-PERP
results.evidence: Code: live.py:29-35 hardcodes SYMBOLS['hyperliquid']='BTC/USDC:USDC', live.py:65 self.symbol=SYMBOLS[self.venue], and p.market.symbol is never used. __main__.py common() gives the 'live' parser --coin BTC/ETH/SOL, cmd_live builds params_for(coin), and runner.run feeds HyperliquidFeed(p.market.symbol), so prices and sizes come from ETH or SOL while orders go to BTC. My repro is v_live.py: a stub exchange, no network, with the mandatory --max-notional 50. The ETH desk sends ('BTC/USDC:USDC','buy',0.02008), about $1,659 of BTC (33x). The SOL desk sends 0.46729 BTC, about $38.6k (770x). The auditor missed something worse: the protective stop goes on BTC at the ETH or SOL price level (trigger 2340.6 for ETH, 100.6 for SOL), so in practice the position has no stop. Positions and balance are also read for BTC. One caveat: Hyperliquid's margin check would probably reject the SOL order, and would reject the ETH order unless the account's BTC leverage is set to about 34x or higher. A rejected order raises an exception, which sets entry_kill. Either way the orders are wrong, and in the worst case the account holds an unstopped BTC position at more than 30x. Live only; paper is unaffected.

results.title: A failed stop placement after a live entry leaves the position with no exchange stop
results.evidence: Repro in v_live.py: the stub rejects the stopLossPrice order. The exception propagates, and afterwards the position is open with local stop 80000 and stop_order_id None. runner.py:109 re-places a stop only when `not position.stop`, which is False here. check_stop_price at a price below the local stop (79000) only syncs, so the position stays open. Correction: 'nothing re-places it' is too strong. Engine._manage calls broker.update_stop, which calls _place_stop, whenever the trail rises. In my instrumented replay (v_misc.py) the trail rose above the initial stop at the first 2h close in 83-86% of trades and within 3 bars in 89-91%, so the stop is usually restored within about 2h. In the 3-6% of trades where the trail never rises before the stop is hit (adverse moves with rising ATR), a live position would have no stop until the slow EMA100/400 flip. That tail is real. The bug only fires on an exchange error at entry. That makes it robustness under the rubric (low), but I kept medium because the downside at up to 5x leverage is the whole account.

results.title: Post-only (maker) entries with a taker chase pass P1-P8 as an execution overlay (modest; about half is modelled slippage)
results.evidence: I wrote my own MakerBroker (v_sims.py, v_neigh.py) using Binance 5m bars rebuilt from the raw zip files (not the auditor's pickles). Fill counts at k=0, W=60: 114/118 BTC, 232/236 ETH, 107/107 SOL, identical to the report. Equal-weight desk: baseline OOS Sharpe 0.854, OOS return 46.33%, 2x-cost return 33.67%. W60 version: IS Sharpe 1.539, OOS Sharpe 0.897, OOS return 49.25%, 2x-cost return 40.89%, max drawdown 14.2%. W15 version: IS 1.539, OOS 0.901, OOS return 49.71%, 2x-cost return 41.26%. OOS correlation with the desk 0.9996-0.9998; 50/50 blend Sharpe 0.875-0.876 vs 0.852 for the desk alone, so P8 passes only via the blend clause. All 6 distinct neighbours: OOS Sharpe 0.883-0.907, all with positive return. My in-sample Sharpe is about 0.01 lower than the auditor's because I drop SOL's pre-listing days; the baseline CSV counts them as 0 (it gives 1.515), and the gap does not change the comparison. P1-P8 hold as written. However, P8's blend clause is met automatically by any cost cut on the same strategy, so this is a fee optimisation, not an edge. I lowered the severity to low because it is an improvement opportunity (about $0.9-1.6 a year on 3 x $50), not a defect or drift. The sub-claim that unfilled entries average +878 bps vs +352 bps was not re-checked, and it rests on only about 4 BTC chases.

verification.summary:
I re-checked all 10 exec_audit findings with my own scripts and data handling, and all of them hold. Two need a correction and two need a different severity. Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c67283e4-8e62-5bce-a0e4-e537e0ac564b/scratchpad/edge/verify/audit_exec_audit_p/ (vc.py, v_replay.py, v_live.py, v_live2.py, v_5m.py, v_poll.py, v_gh.py, v_venue.py, v_sims.py, v_neigh.py, v_misc.py, v_paper.py, hl_live/). I did not run the auditor's scripts because they overwrite their own JSON files, and I loaded none of their pickles. My full replay matches baseline_daily.csv (correlation 1.0; Sharpe in-sample/out-of-sample 1.41/0.88, 0.71/0.52, 0.76/0.24).

Results:
- **Live-broker coin bug (high), confirmed.** It is worse than reported: the stop also goes on BTC at the ETH or SOL price level, so the position effectively has no stop. Hyperliquid's margin check would probably reject the oversized orders, depending on the account's leverage setting.
- **Failed stop placement (medium), confirmed.** "Nothing re-places it" is too strong. The next trail step re-places the stop at the next 2h close in 83-86% of trades. The 3-6% where it never rises are exactly the adverse cases.
- **Maker entries, confirmed.** My own implementation gives the same fills, Sharpes, 2x-cost returns and neighbours. P1-P8 hold as written, but P8 passes only through the blend clause, which any cost cut on the same strategy satisfies. It is a fee saving, not an edge, so I lowered it from medium to low.
- **Slippage, HL funding, venue match, tiny-account effects, paper fill timing, stop fills and the spread/depth gates:** all numbers reproduce, some within definitional noise. The slippage title's "6-25x" ratio should read about 6x to 50x. The paper.py line cite should be 100/119, not 91.
- **Sync booking at the mid, confirmed for the running loop.** The "runner was down" part is wrong: on restart the exit is booked at the local stop.

Extra observation from reading the code, not reproduced: live state files are not per coin (runner.py:64,68 use state/live_desk.json and state/live_position.json). Two live desks started from the same directory would share state.

On your question: more than 2 agents can run the audit. This check was done by a separate agent with its own scripts, and nothing in these findings depends on how many agents run it. I picked no new parameters and took nothing new to out-of-sample; this was verification only.

result.summary:
I audited the live desk code read-only: no repo edits, no network calls, no keys used. All 27 tests pass (python3 -m pytest -q). All repro scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c67283e4-8e62-5bce-a0e4-e537e0ac564b/scratchpad/edge/audit_p/code/.

The main paper path is sound. I replayed the real paper.step() on real Binance 2h data from 2024-01 to 2026-09 with a fake feed. The replay used the real 1500-bar lookback and 4-day funding window, and stepped 1 to 5 bars at a time to imitate missed cron runs. It produced exactly the same trades, cash and funding as the desk's own backtest loop for all three coins:
- BTC: 56 trades, $50 to $100.00
- ETH: 104 trades, $50 to $66.20
- SOL: 52 trades, $50 to $53.63

So the behaviours the brief asked about are all correct and match the backtest:
- The Donchian channel excludes the current bar.
- EMA warm-up has no practical effect.
- Within a bar, entry, stop, trail and trend-flip run in the same order as the backtest.
- Stops are checked against the bar's high/low and fill at the open on a gap.
- Fees and slippage are charged on both sides.
- Funding has the right sign, and its APR units are correct for both Hyperliquid's hourly and Binance's 8-hourly prints.
- Missed bars are processed and stops hit between runs are honoured.
- The workflow has a concurrency group (paper.yml:23-25, cancel-in-progress false), so two runs cannot overlap.

The real defects are elsewhere:
1. HIGH, paper record: in the GitHub workflow, any transient failure of the first ledger fetch is treated as "no ledger yet". The step then opens fresh $50 accounts. If the second fetch in the save step succeeds, those fresh accounts are pushed over the real ones as an ordinary commit, wiping cash, the open position and trade history.
2. HIGH, live (latent): the live broker sends every coin's orders to BTC. Running `live --coin ETH` or `--coin SOL` trades BTC, breaks the --max-notional cap by 31x (ETH) to 547x (SOL), and places the stop at the other coin's price.
3. MEDIUM, live: when the exchange-side stop fills while the loop is away, the trade is booked at the current mid price, not the stop fill. In the repro, a -$4.14 stop-out was booked as a +$2.86 win.
4. MEDIUM, live: after a gap of several bars, the live loop only processes the latest bar, unlike paper, which catches up every missed bar.
5. MEDIUM, paper vs backtest drift: Hyperliquid funding runs about twice Binance's level. As a result the backtest understates funding cost by about 2.5x, and the crowding gate blocks some breakouts in paper that it never blocked in the backtest.
6. LOW: one ledger with the wrong bar interval aborts the whole multi-coin step and skips the save; paper's stale-data gate never fires; trade sizes are not rounded to Hyperliquid's size decimals; a pending order loses its take-profit when the ledger is saved.
7. INFO: EMA seeding on the sliding window, Hyperliquid vs Binance price differences, and funding timestamp attribution all have negligible effect.

None of these defects explains the BTC strategy's -11% in 2026. That result comes from the strategy itself, not from a code defect. The two HIGH items should be fixed before trusting the paper record or arming live trading for ETH or SOL.

findings.title: A transient git-fetch failure silently resets all three paper accounts to a fresh $50
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/paper.yml:39-43: `if git fetch --depth=1 origin paper-ledger; then git checkout FETCH_HEAD -- ledger/; else echo "no paper-ledger branch yet..."` treats ANY fetch error (network blip, 5xx, auth hiccup) as 'branch does not exist'. desk/paper.py:53-94 then opens a new ledger for every coin (meta.last_bar_ts=0, started_ts=now) and emits an event, so changed=true (__main__.py:199-201). The save step (paper.yml:56-82) fetches again; if that succeeds it builds a worktree on the real branch head, copies the fresh ledger/*/paper.json over the real ones and pushes a normal fast-forward commit. Repro output: origin paper-ledger before = cash 63.21, open long, 3 trades, runs 38; after = commit 'ledger: BTC $50.00 ...', cash 50.0, position None, trades 0, runs 1.
findings.impact: Wrong P&L record. The paper experiment's cash, open position (abandoned without an exit), trade history, risk state (peak, halt, cooldown) and started_ts are all reset for BTC, ETH and SOL at once. The 14-day / positive-return paper promotion gate is then measured from the reset. Nothing alerts on it; the old state survives only in git history.
findings.repro: bash /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c67283e4-8e62-5bce-a0e4-e537e0ac564b/scratchpad/edge/audit_p/code/workflow_fetch_failure_wipes_ledger.sh (local bare origin; the Load/Save shell is extracted verbatim from paper.yml; runs the real paper.step with a fake feed)
findings.fix: Tell 'branch missing' apart from 'fetch failed': check `git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin paper-ledger` (exit 2 = missing) and fail the job on any other error. Or retry the fetch and abort if it still fails. Add a guard in the save step: refuse to push a ledger whose meta.started_ts is newer than the branch's, or whose runs/trades count went down, unless a manual flag is set.

findings.title: LiveBroker hard-codes the BTC market for every coin (ETH/SOL live would trade BTC and blow through the notional cap)
findings.evidence: desk/brokers/live.py:29-35 SYMBOLS = {"hyperliquid": "BTC/USDC:USDC", ...} and live.py:65 `self.symbol = SYMBOLS[self.venue]` ignore p.market.symbol. Meanwhile runner.py:213 builds the feed with p.market.symbol, so the desk decides and sizes on ETH/SOL prices while orders go to BTC. The cap at live.py:142-143 divides by the ETH/SOL price. The stop (live.py:187-193) is placed at the ETH/SOL price level on the BTC position. README.md:112-113 documents per-coin go-live, and cmd_live accepts --coin ETH|SOL. Also runner.py:68 uses one state file (state/live_position.json) for every coin. Repro, $50 cap with a $100 intended ticket: ETH sends 0.01923 BTC = $1,576.86 (31.5x the cap) with a sell stop at 2,522; SOL sends 0.33333 BTC = $27,333 (547x the cap) with a sell stop at 145.5, which is effectively no stop.
findings.impact: Wrong instrument and wrong size. The first ETH or SOL live entry would open a BTC position 31-547x the --max-notional cap with a stop that cannot trigger at a sensible level, on a $50 account. Latent: live has not been run yet.
findings.fix: Derive the symbol from the coin, e.g. f"{p.market.symbol}/USDC:USDC" for Hyperliquid (and the matching format per venue). Assert at startup that the market exists and that its base currency equals p.market.symbol. Use a per-coin state file (state/<COIN>/live_position.json). Add a test that LiveBroker(params_for('ETH')).symbol starts with 'ETH'.

findings.title: Live sync books an exchange-side stop at the current mid, not the stop fill (a loss can be recorded as a win)
findings.area: live broker / P&L and risk brakes
findings.evidence: desk/brokers/live.py:103-115: when the exchange shows no position but the desk has one, it books the exit at `px = price or pos.stop` (line 109). runner.py:252 calls broker.check_stop_price(mid, now), which calls sync(mid), so px is the CURRENT mid. The fee is likewise estimated at the mid. Repro: long 0.002 BTC at 80,000 with the stop at 78,000; the stop fills, and price has bounced to 81,500 by the next poll. Booked exit 81,500, net +$2.855; true result at the stop is -$4.142. counted_as_loss=False.
findings.impact: Wrong recorded P&L on every exchange stop-out: the error equals the price move between the fill and the next poll, plus any gap. Booked P&L feeds engine._update_risk, so consecutive losses are undercounted and the 5-loss cooldown can fail to fire. The trade log then differs from the exchange account (cash is re-read from the exchange, so equity itself stays correct).
findings.fix: On reconcile, fetch the stop order or the user's fills (fetch_order(stop_order_id) / fetch_my_trades since entry_ts) and book the actual average fill price and fee. If that is unavailable, book at pos.stop (the resting price), not at the current mid, and flag the trade as estimated.

findings.title: Funding print bar attribution depends on millisecond jitter in the timestamps
findings.evidence: indicators.py:73-90 assigns a print to the bar with open < ts <= open+bar, using raw milliseconds. Hyperliquid prints are almost all late (1.3% exactly on the hour), so they go to the next bar. findings.fix: Round print timestamps to the minute before bucketing (as the harness does), so the attribution rule is deterministic.

verification.summary:
Every one of the auditor's 12 findings reproduced with my own scripts, and I kept all of the auditor's severities. This was a verification, so no strategies were searched (0 trials, 0 finalists taken out of sample). The repo was used read-only, there were no network calls, and pytest passes 27/27. The scripts, PLAN.md and a results log are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c67283e4-8e62-5bce-a0e4-e537e0ac564b/scratchpad/edge/verify/audit_code_audit_p/.

Confirmed:
- HIGH f1: a transient Load-step fetch failure resets all three paper ledgers to $50 and pushes them over the real branch. Shown end to end with the workflow shell taken verbatim from paper.yml and the real step.
- HIGH f2: LiveBroker sends ETH and SOL orders to BTC, at 31.5x and 547x the $50 cap, with stops that cannot trigger at a sensible level (latent).
- MEDIUM f3: an exchange stop fill is booked at the next poll's mid; a -$4.14 loss was recorded as a +$2.85 win.
- MEDIUM f4: after a gap, the live loop passes only the newest bar; 5 bars closed and 1 was processed.
- MEDIUM f5: Hyperliquid funding is about 2x Binance's (median APR 9.75% vs 5.06%), and the crowding gate drops 0.79% of bars vs 0%.
- LOW f6–f9:
  - f6: the SystemExit escape skips every coin and the save.
  - f7: paper's stale-data gate never fires.
  - f8: rounding cuts on size decimals: SOL median 1.88%, max 12.79%.
  - f9: pending orders lose their take-profit across a ledger save and reload.
- INFO f10–f12:
  - f10: paper matches the backtest exactly on 2024-01..2026-09 for all three coins, with 0 trade differences.
  - f11: Hyperliquid and Binance prices give nearly the same trades.
  - f12: funding print attribution depends on millisecond timestamps.

Corrections and nuances:
1. Some line references are wrong. The audit's citations in runner.py, filter.py and feeds/hyperliquid.py point past the end of those files, though the behaviour they describe is real.
2. On the live 2h interval, Hyperliquid funding cost about 2.6x what the backtest charges for trades from 2024-07 ($13.98 vs $5.33). Final equity was still about the same ($173.70 vs $173.67), because the one breakout the gate blocked only on Hyperliquid happened to be an $8.13 loser.
3. My BTC replay ends at $99.74, not the audit's $100.00, likely because of a slightly different window. The paper-equals-backtest result is the same either way.

The auditor's conclusion that no code defect explains BTC's -11% in 2026 is consistent with paper matching the backtest bar for bar. I did not test it separately.
